docs.text: Viewer The interactive viewer and its panels, themes and callbacks ( ernie.app ). Ernie's interactive viewer: a window onto a Scene, driven by run() or step(). Classes: Name Description Demo A demo: a scene built in init , advanced by step, drawn by render and checked by test_final, run by DemoRunner in a window, headless or without a viewer. Subclass ernie.demo.Demo in Python, which adds argparse options and NumPy images. DemoInfo A demo the runner can build, for the Demos panel. DemoOptions The options every demo takes (parse_demo_options), as Newton's examples share theirs. DemoRunner Runs demos as Newton's examples run: in a window, headless or without a viewer, writing --output, running --test checks and reporting --benchmark; in a window a Demos panel switches between the catalogue's demos. Exposure How the viewport exposes its image. FrameInfo Passed to on_frame callbacks. Gizmo What the transform gizmo on a selected prim does. Lighting How the viewport lights the scene. Theme Colours (sRGB RGBA tuples) and metrics of the viewer's UI. Viewer A window onto a Scene: a docked viewport plus panels. Edits from code and from the GUI go through the same scene. Drive it with run(), or call step() from your own loop. ViewportDisplay What the viewport draws over the scene (the eye menu) and its heads-up display lists. Assign a changed copy to Viewer.viewport_display. WidgetPanel A dockable panel of simple widgets; each calls its callback when the user changes it. Functions: Name Description main The ernie program (ernie.cli): the viewer on a scene file or the default scene with a Demos panel of Ernie's C++ demos, or a render without a window; args without the program name. Returns the exit status. parse_demo_options Parses the shared demo options from a command line without the program name, leaving the others in extra; raises ValueError for a bad value. registered_demos The C++ demos compiled in (ERNIE_REGISTER_DEMO), by category and name. Demo Demo(viewer: Viewer | None, options: DemoOptions) A demo: a scene built in init , advanced by step, drawn by render and checked by test_final, run by DemoRunner in a window, headless or without a viewer. Subclass ernie.demo.Demo in Python, which adds argparse options and NumPy images. DemoRunner DemoRunner(options: DemoOptions, title: str = 'Ernie demos') Runs demos as Newton's examples run: in a window, headless or without a viewer, writing --output, running --test checks and reporting --benchmark; in a window a Demos panel switches between the catalogue's demos. Opens the viewer the options ask for (none for --viewer null or --benchmark); demos built from now on register in a scope of their own. Methods: Name Description create Builds the catalogue's demo index for this runner. request_reset Builds the running demo afresh before the next frame, as the panel's Reset does. request_switch Switches to the catalogue's demo index before the next frame, as the Demos panel's menu does. With a viewer only. run Runs demo until its window closes or it has run its frames, then writes --output, runs test_final and reports the benchmark; returns the demo running at the end (the Demos panel may have switched), or None. Closes the viewer. set_catalog The demos the Demos panel lists, and which of them runs first. Attributes: options ( DemoOptions ) – viewer ( Viewer ) – The viewer, or None without one. options property options: DemoOptions viewer property viewer: Viewer The viewer, or None without one. create create(index: int) -> object Builds the catalogue's demo index for this runner. request_reset request_reset() -> None Builds the running demo afresh before the next frame, as the panel's Reset does. request_switch request_switch(index: int) -> None Switches to the catalogue's demo index before the next frame, as the Demos panel's menu does. With a viewer only. run run(demo: Demo) -> object Runs demo until its window closes or it has run its frames, then writes --output, runs test_final and reports the benchmark; returns the demo running at the end (the Demos panel may have switched), or None. Closes the viewer. set_catalog set_catalog(demos: Sequence[DemoInfo], current: int = 0) -> None The demos the Demos panel lists, and which of them runs first. Viewer Viewer( scene: Scene, title: str = "Ernie", width: int = 1600, height: int = 900, hidden: bool = False, validation: bool = False, device: str = "", theme: Theme | None = None, layout: str | PathLike | None = None, settings: Path = ..., renderer: str = "raster", vsync: bool = False, ) A window onto a Scene: a docked viewport plus panels. Edits from code and from the GUI go through the same scene. Drive it with run(), or call step() from your own loop. Opens the window (none when hidden ) on a Vulkan device. Raises RuntimeError without a window system or Vulkan device. Methods: Name Description add_hud_item Adds a line "label: value(viewer)" to the viewport's heads-up display, refreshed a few times a second; value returns a str. Returns an id. add_light_pattern Registers a laser pattern with the viewport's renderer, as Renderer.add_light_pattern does. add_menu_item Adds label to the menu bar's menu ; calls action(viewer). add_overlay_click_handler Calls clicked(viewer, overlay, id) when a click in the viewport lands on a screen overlay item with an id (a button's, Overlay.button ), in place of picking the scene there; the item under the pointer shows its hover colour. Returns an id for remove_viewport_item . add_overlay_pick_handler Calls picked(viewer, hit) when a click in the viewport lands on an overlay item in the world (an OverlayHit : a marker, a line, a batch's item), in place of picking the scene there. Returns an id for remove_viewport_item . add_panel Adds a WidgetPanel titled title , docked at dock in the default layout. add_viewport_menu_item Adds label to the viewport's settings menu; calls action(viewer), and shows a check while checked(viewer) returns True. Returns an id. add_viewport_toggle Adds a toggle to the viewport's eye menu, such as for physics contacts or labels. With overlay , it shows and hides that scene overlay in the viewport; changed(viewer, shown) is told when the user switches it. Returns an id. camera_from_view Defines a Camera prim at path with the active camera's pose and lens. capture Writes the next viewport frame to path as PNG. capture_window Writes the whole window, UI and all, as PNG; hidden viewers only. clear_attribute Clears an attribute back to its fallback, as an undoable GUI edit. clear_log clear_scene Empties the stage for new content: removes every prim but the viewer's own and every overlay but its own, clears the selection and undo history, and forgets the settings, camera and lighting set. Call reset_session once the new content is in. close creatable_types The prim types create and the Create menu make. create Creates a prim of type (any of creatable_types ) with defaults that make it show, as one undo step; selects it and returns its path. delete Deletes prims and their descendants as one undo step. duplicate Copies prims with their descendants beside themselves ( _01, ...) as one undo step; selects and returns the copies. edit Sets an attribute as an undoable GUI edit. evict_textures Drops every texture the viewport's materials read, as Renderer.evict_textures does. focus_panel Shows the panel titled title and brings it to the front of its dock. frame Frames paths (the whole scene when empty) with the active camera. has_light_pattern Whether the viewport's renderer has light pattern id . hud_item_shown load_layout log Adds a message to the Log panel. log_array Logs array, (n) or (rows, cols) numbers from any framework, on the CPU or the GPU, as a heatmap in the Plots panel, replacing the last (Newton's log_array). log_image Logs image in a panel of its own titled name, replacing the last (Newton's log_image): (rows, cols), (rows, cols, channels) or a batch (views, rows, cols, channels), with 1, 3 or 4 channels, uint8 (0 to 255, shown as they are) or float32 (0 to 1), from any DLPack framework (NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, Warp, CuPy). A CUDA image is copied device to device into the panel's texture after the work queued on stream, without the host; map_image writes the texture itself, with no copy. log_scalar Logs value as the next sample of the scalar signal name, drawn as a line of its last thousand samples in the Plots panel (Newton's log_scalar). clear drops the samples before; smoothing averages that many values into each sample. logged_scalars The samples of scalar signal name so far, oldest first. look_at Puts the active camera at eye looking at target (z up), which it then orbits and zooms towards. map As Renderer.map, for the viewer's scene and renderer: a CUDA array over the viewer's own memory for the attribute, to write in place and then scene.unmap(path, attribute, stream) ; map again every frame. map_image The texture of image panel name itself, as a writable CUDA array of shape (as log_image takes, with 1 or 4 channels) and dtype: write it on stream (with Warp, PyTorch, CuPy...), then unmap_image(name, stream), and the panel shows it with no copy at all. Its rows are the texture's pitch apart (see its strides). Map again for each new image. new_scope A registration scope not used before (see scope), without making it current. on_frame Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) at the start of every frame, before the UI; returns an id for remove_callback. on_post_render Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) after the frame is submitted and presented; its edits show in the next frame. Returns an id. on_pre_render Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) after the UI, just before the scene is synced and rendered, so its edits show in this frame; returns an id. on_selection Calls callback(viewer, paths) when the selection changes; returns an id. open_scene Replaces the stage with the scene a JSON file describes (the format of ernie.load_scene and ernie.save_scene), as File > Open Scene does: removes every prim but the viewer's own and every overlay but its own, loads the file and starts the session over (clear_scene, then reset_session). A file that does not load raises ValueError and leaves the stage as it was. panel_visible Whether the panel titled title (such as "Profiler") shows. pause Pauses the timeline where it is. pick The prim the viewport shows at pixel (x, y) of its last frame; an empty Path for the background. play Plays the timeline: each frame advances the stage's time code, before the on_frame callbacks. record_sequence Records the timeline's frames from start to end (its range by default), every every frames, a frame a step, as PNGs in a folder of the capture folder; then encodes them with ffmpeg into video ("mp4", "prores" or "none") in the background. redo Redoes the last undone GUI edit. redraw Counts as a change for eco mode: for what changes the image outside the scene, such as GPU arrays written in place. remove_callback remove_logged Forgets the scalar signal, array or image name. remove_panel remove_scope Removes everything added in scope; built-in panels are only hidden. remove_viewport_item Removes a viewport toggle, heads-up display item or viewport menu item. rename Renames a prim, moving its descendants, as one undo step; returns its new path. reset_session Starts over on the scene's present content once it has been replaced, as open_scene and the demo runner do: clears the selection and undo history, and picks the RenderSettings, the camera (perspective_camera, framing the scene) and the lighting as on opening, except those set (settings, active_camera, lighting) since clear_scene or opening. run Draws frames until the window closes or close() is called. save_layout save_scene Writes the stage, every prim but the viewer's own, to path as JSON (ernie.save_scene), as File > Save Scene As does. screenshot Saves the next viewport frame as PNG in the capture folder (as F10 does): the image with the scene's overlays, without the viewer's UI. Returns its path. set_hud_item_shown set_panel_visible Shows or hides the panel titled title , as the Window menu does. set_viewport_toggle_shown step Draws one frame; returns whether the window is still open. step_clock Advances the sensor clock by seconds at the next frame, paused or not. step_frames Pauses the timeline and moves it frames frames on (back for negative), within its range. stop Pauses the timeline, back at its range's start. stop_recording Ends the recording, encoding what it wrote. sync Syncs the scene into the renderer now; raises ValueError for data it cannot use. undo Undoes the last GUI edit; returns whether there was one. unmap_image Ends writing image name (map_image): frames show it after the work queued on stream. viewport_toggle_shown Attributes: active_camera ( Path ) – auto_exposing ( bool ) – cameras ( list [ Path ] ) – The viewer's cameras, then the scene's, by path. capture_folder ( Path ) – Where screenshots and sequences go; made when first written to. capture_name ( str ) – Capture file names without extension: {scene}, {camera}, {date} and {time} fill in. capture_scale ( float ) – The rendered size over the viewport's render resolution, such as 2 or 4 for stills larger than the screen. capture_vars ( list [ str ] ) – The render vars a capture writes, rendered anew through the active camera: LdrColor as PNG, the others as EXR named _ . Empty writes the viewport's image as shown. clock_paused ( bool ) – Whether the sensor clock stands still between frames; by default it runs with them. device_name ( str ) – eco_paused ( bool ) – Whether eco mode (RenderSettings ernie:ecoMode:enabled, as Omniverse's) has paused the viewport's rendering, nothing having changed for ernie:ecoMode:maxFramesWithoutChange frames. encoding ( bool ) – Whether a sequence's video is still encoding. exposure ( Exposure ) – exposure_compensation ( float ) – Stops on top of either exposure mode. gizmo ( Gizmo ) – gizmo_local ( bool ) – is_open ( bool ) – lighting ( Lighting ) – log_entries ( list [ tuple [ float , str , str ]] ) – (seconds, level, text) of every message in the log. looping ( bool ) – Whether playing past the range's end starts over at its start; otherwise it stops there. On by default. metered_ev ( float | None ) – EV100 of the scene's average luminance as last metered, or None. minimal ( bool | None ) – Whether the viewport shades minimally (Kit's RTX - Minimal), overriding the render settings' ernie:minimal:mode; None follows them. minimal_shown ( bool ) – Whether the viewport shades minimally now. perspective_camera ( Final [ Path ] ) – (arg: object, /) -> ernie._ernie.Path play_every_frame ( bool ) – Whether playing advances a frame each step however long it took (and the sensor clock a frame's seconds), rather than real time. playing ( bool ) – Whether the timeline is playing. recent_captures ( list [ Path ] ) – The files captured since the viewer opened, latest last. recording ( bool ) – Whether a sequence is recording. recording_progress ( tuple [ int , int ] ) – A recording sequence's frames written and all. renderer ( str ) – The render backend the viewport draws with; assign to switch. renderers ( Final [ list [ str ]] ) – The render backends the viewer can switch between. scene ( Scene ) – scope ( int ) – The registration scope: callbacks, panels, menu items and viewport items added belong to it, and remove_scope removes them all at once, as the demo runner does switching demos. 0, the default, is the application's own. selection ( list [ Path ] ) – session_root ( Final [ Path ] ) – (arg: object, /) -> ernie._ernie.Path settings ( Path ) – theme ( Theme ) – time_code ( float ) – The stage's time code, which the timeline plays. view_band ( int ) – The spectral band shown of SpectralRadiance, or -1 for their mean. view_var ( str ) – The render var the viewport shows, one of view_vars . view_vars ( list [ str ] ) – The render vars the current renderer can show in the viewport, with the AOVs of the viewport's sensor filter chain as 'aov: '. viewport_display ( ViewportDisplay ) – What the viewport draws over the scene and its heads-up display lists. vsync ( bool ) – Whether frames wait for the display's refresh; off draws as fast as it renders. docs.text: The interactive viewer and its panels, themes and callbacks ( ernie.app ). Ernie's interactive viewer: a window onto a Scene, driven by run() or step(). Classes: Name Description Demo A demo: a scene built in init , advanced by step, drawn by render and checked by test_final, run by DemoRunner in a window, headless or without a viewer. Subclass ernie.demo.Demo in Python, which adds argparse options and NumPy images. DemoInfo A demo the runner can build, for the Demos panel. DemoOptions The options every demo takes (parse_demo_options), as Newton's examples share theirs. DemoRunner Runs demos as Newton's examples run: in a window, headless or without a viewer, writing --output, running --test checks and reporting --benchmark; in a window a Demos panel switches between the catalogue's demos. Exposure How the viewport exposes its image. FrameInfo Passed to on_frame callbacks. Gizmo What the transform gizmo on a selected prim does. Lighting How the viewport lights the scene. Theme Colours (sRGB RGBA tuples) and metrics of the viewer's UI. Viewer A window onto a Scene: a docked viewport plus panels. Edits from code and from the GUI go through the same scene. Drive it with run(), or call step() from your own loop. ViewportDisplay What the viewport draws over the scene (the eye menu) and its heads-up display lists. Assign a changed copy to Viewer.viewport_display. WidgetPanel A dockable panel of simple widgets; each calls its callback when the user changes it. docs.text: DemoRunner(options: DemoOptions, title: str = 'Ernie demos') Runs demos as Newton's examples run: in a window, headless or without a viewer, writing --output, running --test checks and reporting --benchmark; in a window a Demos panel switches between the catalogue's demos. Opens the viewer the options ask for (none for --viewer null or --benchmark); demos built from now on register in a scope of their own. Methods: Name Description create Builds the catalogue's demo index for this runner. request_reset Builds the running demo afresh before the next frame, as the panel's Reset does. request_switch Switches to the catalogue's demo index before the next frame, as the Demos panel's menu does. With a viewer only. run Runs demo until its window closes or it has run its frames, then writes --output, runs test_final and reports the benchmark; returns the demo running at the end (the Demos panel may have switched), or None. Closes the viewer. set_catalog The demos the Demos panel lists, and which of them runs first. Attributes: options ( DemoOptions ) – viewer ( Viewer ) – The viewer, or None without one.

docs.text: Viewer( scene: Scene, title: str = "Ernie", width: int = 1600, height: int = 900, hidden: bool = False, validation: bool = False, device: str = "", theme: Theme | None = None, layout: str | PathLike | None = None, settings: Path = ..., renderer: str = "raster", vsync: bool = False, ) A window onto a Scene: a docked viewport plus panels. Edits from code and from the GUI go through the same scene. Drive it with run(), or call step() from your own loop. Opens the window (none when hidden ) on a Vulkan device. Raises RuntimeError without a window system or Vulkan device. Methods: Name Description add_hud_item Adds a line "label: value(viewer)" to the viewport's heads-up display, refreshed a few times a second; value returns a str. Returns an id. add_light_pattern Registers a laser pattern with the viewport's renderer, as Renderer.add_light_pattern does. add_menu_item Adds label to the menu bar's menu ; calls action(viewer). add_overlay_click_handler Calls clicked(viewer, overlay, id) when a click in the viewport lands on a screen overlay item with an id (a button's, Overlay.button ), in place of picking the scene there; the item under the pointer shows its hover colour. Returns an id for remove_viewport_item . add_overlay_pick_handler Calls picked(viewer, hit) when a click in the viewport lands on an overlay item in the world (an OverlayHit : a marker, a line, a batch's item), in place of picking the scene there. Returns an id for remove_viewport_item . add_panel Adds a WidgetPanel titled title , docked at dock in the default layout. add_viewport_menu_item Adds label to the viewport's settings menu; calls action(viewer), and shows a check while checked(viewer) returns True. Returns an id. add_viewport_toggle Adds a toggle to the viewport's eye menu, such as for physics contacts or labels. With overlay , it shows and hides that scene overlay in the viewport; changed(viewer, shown) is told when the user switches it. Returns an id. camera_from_view Defines a Camera prim at path with the active camera's pose and lens. capture Writes the next viewport frame to path as PNG. capture_window Writes the whole window, UI and all, as PNG; hidden viewers only. clear_attribute Clears an attribute back to its fallback, as an undoable GUI edit. clear_log clear_scene Empties the stage for new content: removes every prim but the viewer's own and every overlay but its own, clears the selection and undo history, and forgets the settings, camera and lighting set. Call reset_session once the new content is in. close creatable_types The prim types create and the Create menu make. create Creates a prim of type (any of creatable_types ) with defaults that make it show, as one undo step; selects it and returns its path. delete Deletes prims and their descendants as one undo step. duplicate Copies prims with their descendants beside themselves ( _01, ...) as one undo step; selects and returns the copies. edit Sets an attribute as an undoable GUI edit. evict_textures Drops every texture the viewport's materials read, as Renderer.evict_textures does. focus_panel Shows the panel titled title and brings it to the front of its dock. frame Frames paths (the whole scene when empty) with the active camera. has_light_pattern Whether the viewport's renderer has light pattern id . hud_item_shown load_layout log Adds a message to the Log panel. log_array Logs array, (n) or (rows, cols) numbers from any framework, on the CPU or the GPU, as a heatmap in the Plots panel, replacing the last (Newton's log_array). log_image Logs image in a panel of its own titled name, replacing the last (Newton's log_image): (rows, cols), (rows, cols, channels) or a batch (views, rows, cols, channels), with 1, 3 or 4 channels, uint8 (0 to 255, shown as they are) or float32 (0 to 1), from any DLPack framework (NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, Warp, CuPy). A CUDA image is copied device to device into the panel's texture after the work queued on stream, without the host; map_image writes the texture itself, with no copy. log_scalar Logs value as the next sample of the scalar signal name, drawn as a line of its last thousand samples in the Plots panel (Newton's log_scalar). clear drops the samples before; smoothing averages that many values into each sample. logged_scalars The samples of scalar signal name so far, oldest first. look_at Puts the active camera at eye looking at target (z up), which it then orbits and zooms towards. map As Renderer.map, for the viewer's scene and renderer: a CUDA array over the viewer's own memory for the attribute, to write in place and then scene.unmap(path, attribute, stream) ; map again every frame. map_image The texture of image panel name itself, as a writable CUDA array of shape (as log_image takes, with 1 or 4 channels) and dtype: write it on stream (with Warp, PyTorch, CuPy...), then unmap_image(name, stream), and the panel shows it with no copy at all. Its rows are the texture's pitch apart (see its strides). Map again for each new image. new_scope A registration scope not used before (see scope), without making it current. on_frame Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) at the start of every frame, before the UI; returns an id for remove_callback. on_post_render Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) after the frame is submitted and presented; its edits show in the next frame. Returns an id. on_pre_render Calls callback(viewer, frame_info) after the UI, just before the scene is synced and rendered, so its edits show in this frame; returns an id. on_selection Calls callback(viewer, paths) when the selection changes; returns an id. open_scene Replaces the stage with the scene a JSON file describes (the format of ernie.load_scene and ernie.save_scene), as File > Open Scene does: removes every prim but the viewer's own and every overlay but its own, loads the file and starts the session over (clear_scene, then reset_session). A file that does not load raises ValueError and leaves the stage as it was. panel_visible Whether the panel titled title (such as "Profiler") shows. pause Pauses the timeline where it is. pick The prim the viewport shows at pixel (x, y) of its last frame; an empty Path for the background. play Plays the timeline: each frame advances the stage's time code, before the on_frame callbacks. record_sequence Records the timeline's frames from start to end (its range by default), every every frames, a frame a step, as PNGs in a folder of the capture folder; then encodes them with ffmpeg into video ("mp4", "prores" or "none") in the background. redo Redoes the last undone GUI edit. redraw Counts as a change for eco mode: for what changes the image outside the scene, such as GPU arrays written in place. remove_callback remove_logged Forgets the scalar signal, array or image name. remove_panel remove_scope Removes everything added in scope; built-in panels are only hidden. remove_viewport_item Removes a viewport toggle, heads-up display item or viewport menu item. rename Renames a prim, moving its descendants, as one undo step; returns its new path. reset_session Starts over on the scene's present content once it has been replaced, as open_scene and the demo runner do: clears the selection and undo history, and picks the RenderSettings, the camera (perspective_camera, framing the scene) and the lighting as on opening, except those set (settings, active_camera, lighting) since clear_scene or opening. run Draws frames until the window closes or close() is called. save_layout save_scene Writes the stage, every prim but the viewer's own, to path as JSON (ernie.save_scene), as File > Save Scene As does. screenshot Saves the next viewport frame as PNG in the capture folder (as F10 does): the image with the scene's overlays, without the viewer's UI. Returns its path. set_hud_item_shown set_panel_visible Shows or hides the panel titled title , as the Window menu does. set_viewport_toggle_shown step Draws one frame; returns whether the window is still open. step_clock Advances the sensor clock by seconds at the next frame, paused or not. step_frames Pauses the timeline and moves it frames frames on (back for negative), within its range. stop Pauses the timeline, back at its range's start. stop_recording Ends the recording, encoding what it wrote. sync Syncs the scene into the renderer now; raises ValueError for data it cannot use. undo Undoes the last GUI edit; returns whether there was one. unmap_image Ends writing image name (map_image): frames show it after the work queued on stream. viewport_toggle_shown Attributes: active_camera ( Path ) – auto_exposing ( bool ) – cameras ( list [ Path ] ) – The viewer's cameras, then the scene's, by path. capture_folder ( Path ) – Where screenshots and sequences go; made when first written to. capture_name ( str ) – Capture file names without extension: {scene}, {camera}, {date} and {time} fill in. capture_scale ( float ) – The rendered size over the viewport's render resolution, such as 2 or 4 for stills larger than the screen. capture_vars ( list [ str ] ) – The render vars a capture writes, rendered anew through the active camera: LdrColor as PNG, the others as EXR named _ . Empty writes the viewport's image as shown. clock_paused ( bool ) – Whether the sensor clock stands still between frames; by default it runs with them. device_name ( str ) – eco_paused ( bool ) – Whether eco mode (RenderSettings ernie:ecoMode:enabled, as Omniverse's) has paused the viewport's rendering, nothing having changed for ernie:ecoMode:maxFramesWithoutChange frames. encoding ( bool ) – Whether a sequence's video is still encoding. exposure ( Exposure ) – exposure_compensation ( float ) – Stops on top of either exposure mode. gizmo ( Gizmo ) – gizmo_local ( bool ) – is_open ( bool ) – lighting ( Lighting ) – log_entries ( list [ tuple [ float , str , str ]] ) – (seconds, level, text) of every message in the log. looping ( bool ) – Whether playing past the range's end starts over at its start; otherwise it stops there. On by default. metered_ev ( float | None ) – EV100 of the scene's average luminance as last metered, or None. minimal ( bool | None ) – Whether the viewport shades minimally (Kit's RTX - Minimal), overriding the render settings' ernie:minimal:mode; None follows them. minimal_shown ( bool ) – Whether the viewport shades minimally now. perspective_camera ( Final [ Path ] ) – (arg: object, /) -> ernie._ernie.Path play_every_frame ( bool ) – Whether playing advances a frame each step however long it took (and the sensor clock a frame's seconds), rather than real time. playing ( bool ) – Whether the timeline is playing. recent_captures ( list [ Path ] ) – The files captured since the viewer opened, latest last. recording ( bool ) – Whether a sequence is recording. recording_progress ( tuple [ int , int ] ) – A recording sequence's frames written and all. renderer ( str ) – The render backend the viewport draws with; assign to switch. renderers ( Final [ list [ str ]] ) – The render backends the viewer can switch between. scene ( Scene ) – scope ( int ) – The registration scope: callbacks, panels, menu items and viewport items added belong to it, and remove_scope removes them all at once, as the demo runner does switching demos. 0, the default, is the application's own. selection ( list [ Path ] ) – session_root ( Final [ Path ] ) – (arg: object, /) -> ernie._ernie.Path settings ( Path ) – theme ( Theme ) – time_code ( float ) – The stage's time code, which the timeline plays. view_band ( int ) – The spectral band shown of SpectralRadiance, or -1 for their mean. view_var ( str ) – The render var the viewport shows, one of view_vars . view_vars ( list [ str ] ) – The render vars the current renderer can show in the viewport, with the AOVs of the viewport's sensor filter chain as 'aov: '. viewport_display ( ViewportDisplay ) – What the viewport draws over the scene and its heads-up display lists. vsync ( bool ) – Whether frames wait for the display's refresh; off draws as fast as it renders. Always False for a hidden viewer. wireframe ( Wireframe | None ) – The viewport's Wireframe mode, overriding the render settings' own; None follows them.

docs.text: Batched cameras One camera rendering a view per environment for reinforcement learning ( ernie.batch ). Batched cameras for reinforcement learning: one camera renders a view per environment, each from its own pose of its own world, and every step hands back the observations as GPU arrays. import ernie from ernie.batch import BatchCamera renderer = ernie.Renderer() # environments cloned under Xforms with world=0, 1, ... # (see Scene.clone) scene = ... camera = BatchCamera( renderer, scene, "/World/Camera", views=4096, resolution=(64, 64), render_vars=("LdrColor", "DistanceToCamera"), ) camera.set_worlds(numpy.arange(4096, dtype=numpy.int32)) stream = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream for step in range(steps): # (4096, 4, 4) float32, e.g. a CUDA tensor poses = simulator.camera_poses() observations = camera.step(poses, stream=stream) # (4096, 64, 64, 3) uint8 rgb = torch.from_dlpack(observations["LdrColor"])[..., :3] Nothing waits on the host: poses written as a contiguous float32 CUDA array stay on the GPU ( tokens.POSES_DEVICE ), the render is submitted and the next step is prepared while it runs, and the observations are ready for work queued on stream after the call. Each step's arrays belong to that step's frame: keep them as long as needed, but drop them before many more steps, or each step renders into a frame of its own. Observation shapes: LdrColor (views, rows, cols, 4) uint8 sRGB; HdrColor, Electrons and Normal (views, rows, cols, 4) float32; DistanceToCamera and DistanceToImagePlane (views, rows, cols) float32; PrimId and InstanceId (views, rows, cols) uint32; RawDN (views, rows, cols, 4) uint16; SpectralRadiance (views, bands, rows, cols) float32. Only the vars asked for are rendered and held. References: - B. Shacklett et al., "An Extensible, Data-Oriented Architecture for High-Performance, Many-World Simulation", SIGGRAPH 2023 (Madrona's batch renderer). https://madrona-engine.github.io/ - M. Mittal et al., "Orbit: A Unified Simulation Framework for Interactive Robot Learning Environments", IEEE RA-L 2023 (Isaac Lab's tiled cameras). https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/ Classes: Name Description BatchCamera A batch of views views through the Camera prim camera of __all__ module-attribute __all__ = ['BatchCamera'] BatchCamera BatchCamera( renderer: Renderer, scene: Scene, camera: str | Path, views: int, *, resolution: tuple[int, int] = (64, 64), render_vars: Iterable[str] = ("LdrColor",), product: str | Path = "/Render/BatchCamera", minimal: str | None = None, minimal_color: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, ) A batch of views views through the Camera prim camera of scene , rendered by renderer as the render product product at resolution (columns, rows) with render_vars . The camera keeps its lens and sensor; each view replaces its transform with a pose under the camera's parent ( tokens.POSES ) and sees one world ( tokens.WORLDS ) besides what every world shares, or every world for -1. A missing camera is defined with default settings. Until the first poses, every view takes the camera's own transform, and views see every world. minimal draws the product with minimal shading ( tokens.MINIMAL_MODE ) for throughput: "none" (black, for distances, normals and ids alone), "constantDiffuse" ( minimal_color lit by the sun and ambient), "texturedDiffuse" (surfaces' diffuse colours so lit) or "diffuseGlossyEmission" (those with glossy highlights and emission), in one forward pass straight into the observations, which then map to CUDA without a copy. Methods: Name Description map_poses The views' poses as a writable CUDA array over the set_poses Sets every view's camera-to-world pose under the camera's set_worlds Sets the world each view sees ( tokens.WORLD of the step Renders a step, after setting poses and worlds when Attributes: camera – product – render_vars – renderer – resolution – scene – views – camera instance-attribute camera = Path(str(camera)) product instance-attribute product = Path(str(product)) render_vars instance-attribute render_vars = tuple(render_vars) renderer instance-attribute renderer = renderer resolution instance-attribute resolution = (int(resolution[0]), int(resolution[1])) scene instance-attribute scene = scene views instance-attribute views = int(views) map_poses map_poses(stream: Any = None) -> Any The views' poses as a writable CUDA array over the renderer's own memory, holding the poses as they are: write the next step's poses into it on stream and call step() without poses, and nothing is copied. Map again each step. Needs poses written on the GPU first (a contiguous float32 CUDA array, as set_poses takes). set_poses set_poses(poses: Any, stream: Any = None) -> None Sets every view's camera-to-world pose under the camera's parent: a (views, 4, 4) array in the math convention (translation in the last column) from any DLPack framework. Contiguous float32 CUDA arrays stay on the GPU, copied after the work queued on stream . set_worlds set_worlds(worlds: Any, stream: Any = None) -> None Sets the world each view sees ( tokens.WORLD of the environments' prims): a (views,) int32 array, -1 for every world. A CUDA array is copied to the host once per write, after the work queued on stream , for planning the views' shadows. step step( poses: Any = None, worlds: Any = None, *, stream: Any = None, device: str = "cuda" ) -> Mapping[str, Any] Renders a step, after setting poses and worlds when given, and returns each render var's observations by name. With device="cuda", the arrays are in GPU memory (DLPack, e.g. torch.from_dlpack) and the call returns once the step is submitted: work queued on CUDA stream stream (a CUstream handle or DLPack stream number, default the legacy stream) after it sees the finished render. With device="cpu", it waits for the render and returns NumPy arrays.

docs.text: One camera rendering a view per environment for reinforcement learning ( ernie.batch ). Batched cameras for reinforcement learning: one camera renders a view per environment, each from its own pose of its own world, and every step hands back the observations as GPU arrays. import ernie from ernie.batch import BatchCamera renderer = ernie.Renderer() # environments cloned under Xforms with world=0, 1, ... # (see Scene.clone) scene = ... camera = BatchCamera( renderer, scene, "/World/Camera", views=4096, resolution=(64, 64), render_vars=("LdrColor", "DistanceToCamera"), ) camera.set_worlds(numpy.arange(4096, dtype=numpy.int32)) stream = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream for step in range(steps): # (4096, 4, 4) float32, e.g. a CUDA tensor poses = simulator.camera_poses() observations = camera.step(poses, stream=stream) # (4096, 64, 64, 3) uint8 rgb = torch.from_dlpack(observations["LdrColor"])[..., :3] Nothing waits on the host: poses written as a contiguous float32 CUDA array stay on the GPU ( tokens.POSES_DEVICE ), the render is submitted and the next step is prepared while it runs, and the observations are ready for work queued on stream after the call. Each step's arrays belong to that step's frame: keep them as long as needed, but drop them before many more steps, or each step renders into a frame of its own. Observation shapes: LdrColor (views, rows, cols, 4) uint8 sRGB; HdrColor, Electrons and Normal (views, rows, cols, 4) float32; DistanceToCamera and DistanceToImagePlane (views, rows, cols) float32; PrimId and InstanceId (views, rows, cols) uint32; RawDN (views, rows, cols, 4) uint16; SpectralRadiance (views, bands, rows, cols) float32. Only the vars asked for are rendered and held. References: - B. Shacklett et al., "An Extensible, Data-Oriented Architecture for High-Performance, Many-World Simulation", SIGGRAPH 2023 (Madrona's batch renderer). https://madrona-engine.github.io/ - M. Mittal et al., "Orbit: A Unified Simulation Framework for Interactive Robot Learning Environments", IEEE RA-L 2023 (Isaac Lab's tiled cameras). https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/ Classes: Name Description BatchCamera A batch of views views through the Camera prim camera of

docs.text: BatchCamera( renderer: Renderer, scene: Scene, camera: str | Path, views: int, *, resolution: tuple[int, int] = (64, 64), render_vars: Iterable[str] = ("LdrColor",), product: str | Path = "/Render/BatchCamera", minimal: str | None = None, minimal_color: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, ) A batch of views views through the Camera prim camera of scene , rendered by renderer as the render product product at resolution (columns, rows) with render_vars . The camera keeps its lens and sensor; each view replaces its transform with a pose under the camera's parent ( tokens.POSES ) and sees one world ( tokens.WORLDS ) besides what every world shares, or every world for -1. A missing camera is defined with default settings. Until the first poses, every view takes the camera's own transform, and views see every world. minimal draws the product with minimal shading ( tokens.MINIMAL_MODE ) for throughput: "none" (black, for distances, normals and ids alone), "constantDiffuse" ( minimal_color lit by the sun and ambient), "texturedDiffuse" (surfaces' diffuse colours so lit) or "diffuseGlossyEmission" (those with glossy highlights and emission), in one forward pass straight into the observations, which then map to CUDA without a copy. docs.text: map_poses(stream: Any = None) -> Any The views' poses as a writable CUDA array over the renderer's own memory, holding the poses as they are: write the next step's poses into it on stream and call step() without poses, and nothing is copied. Map again each step. Needs poses written on the GPU first (a contiguous float32 CUDA array, as set_poses takes).

docs.text: set_poses(poses: Any, stream: Any = None) -> None Sets every view's camera-to-world pose under the camera's parent: a (views, 4, 4) array in the math convention (translation in the last column) from any DLPack framework. Contiguous float32 CUDA arrays stay on the GPU, copied after the work queued on stream .
docs.title: set_poses

docs.text: set_worlds(worlds: Any, stream: Any = None) -> None Sets the world each view sees ( tokens.WORLD of the environments' prims): a (views,) int32 array, -1 for every world. A CUDA array is copied to the host once per write, after the work queued on stream , for planning the views' shadows.
docs.title: set_worlds

docs.text: step( poses: Any = None, worlds: Any = None, *, stream: Any = None, device: str = "cuda" ) -> Mapping[str, Any] Renders a step, after setting poses and worlds when given, and returns each render var's observations by name. With device="cuda", the arrays are in GPU memory (DLPack, e.g. torch.from_dlpack) and the call returns once the step is submitted: work queued on CUDA stream stream (a CUstream handle or DLPack stream number, default the legacy stream) after it sees the finished render. With device="cpu", it waits for the render and returns NumPy arrays.

The defocus filter blurs by the axial colour; the lens resamples each band by the lateral. camera is a str, Path, Prim or typed prim.

docs.text: download(url, path, report=print, progress=None) Downloads url to path , its directory made as needed: streamed into path + ".part", renamed when complete. A part left by a download stopped or failed before is resumed (an HTTP range request; from the start if the server ignores it), and failed attempts resume up to five times, going to report . progress , when given, is kept up to date: its bytes in hand, its total (0 until the server says), and its cancelled , which stops the download ( DownloadCancelled ).
docs.title: download

docs.text: fetch_ranges(url, ranges) The bytes of ranges [(first, last), ...] of url , each inclusive, in one request (HTTP range requests; several come back as multipart/byteranges, RFC 9110 section 14.6).
docs.title: fetch_ranges

docs.text: heatmap(values, low, high) values from low (blue) through cyan, green and yellow to high (red), as RGB uint8.
docs.title: heatmap

docs.text: init(parser=None, title='Ernie demos') Parses the command line and opens the viewer it asks for: (viewer, args) , with viewer an ernie.app.Viewer on a new Scene, or None under --viewer null and --benchmark . The runner ( ernie.app.DemoRunner ) rides along in the arguments for run .
docs.title: init

docs.text: load_demo_class(path) Imports the demo file at path afresh (its directory first on sys.path, for the helpers beside it) and returns its Demo class.
docs.title: load_demo_class

docs.text: main(demo_class) Runs demo_class from the command line: run(demo_class(*init(...)), args) .
docs.title: main

docs.text: mean_linear_rgb(image) The mean colour of a uint8 (rows, cols, 3 or 4) image, decoded from sRGB to linear.
docs.title: mean_linear_rgb

docs.text: options_from_args(args) The ernie.app.DemoOptions the parsed arguments of create_parser describe.
docs.title: options_from_args

docs.text: run(demo, args) Steps and renders demo until its window closes or it has run --num-frames , then writes --output , runs its final test and reports the benchmark. In a window the Demos panel lists the demo files beside this one. Returns the demo running at the end.
docs.title: run

docs.text: side_by_side(images, gap=4) uint8 (rows, cols, channels) images of one height next to each other with black gaps.
docs.title: side_by_side

docs.text: srgb_to_linear(rgb) An sRGB-encoded colour in [0, 1] to linear.

docs.text: Rendering Rendering scenes and render products, and reading their outputs on the host or the GPU. Renderer Renderer(backend: str = 'raster', validation: bool = False, device: str = '') Renders a Scene's terrain, meshes, materials, lights, cameras and render settings on a GPU, with one of Ernie's render backends. Opens a GPU, preferring one whose name contains device , with the Vulkan validation layer when validation is set and it is installed, and the render backend (see backends ) on it. Raises RuntimeError without a Vulkan device and ValueError for an unknown backend. Methods: Name Description add_light_pattern Registers a laser pattern written in Slang, for LaserLights to name in ernie:laser:pattern: struct type_name in module slang (which may import light_pattern; ) implementing ILightPattern, whose float emission(LightPatternInput input, LightPatternParams p) gives the relative power per unit area of the tangent plane at input.t = (x / z, y / z), averaged over input.footprint of it (input.beam being the beam's own radius there, for beamlet ); any scale, as Ernie integrates it over |t| < extent so the laser emits its power, unless normalized says it integrates to 1. params is {name: default} in order, or a list of {"name", "default", "description"}; LaserLights set them in ernie:laser:pattern:params, read with p.get(i), and their ernie:laser:pattern:data and ernie:laser:pattern:image are p.data(i) and p.image(uv, footprint). Raises ValueError for an invalid pattern or one that fails to compile, with the compiler's diagnostics. add_sensor_filter Registers a sensor filter written in Slang, for SensorFilter prims to name in ernie:filter:type: struct type_name in module slang implementing IBandFilter (kind="band", on the spectrum), IPixelFilter (kind="pixel", domain "electrons", "digital", "rgb" or "display"), or for kind="spatial", which reads the pixels around its own through a SpatialImage, ISpatialBandFilter (domain "spectrum") or ISpatialPixelFilter (the others), with a nested Params struct of one float per parameter. params is {name: default} in order, or a list of {"name", "default", "description"}; prims set them as inputs: . Raises ValueError for an invalid filter or one that fails to compile, with the compiler's diagnostics. add_temperature_model Registers a temperature model written in Slang, for materials to name in ernie:thermal:model: struct type_name in module slang (which may import temperature_model; ) implementing ITemperatureModel, whose float kelvin(TemperatureInput input, TemperatureParams p) gives a pixel's temperature from its point and normal, the sunlight on it, the material's absorptivity, emissivity and own temperature, and the time. params is {name: default} in order, or a list of {"name", "default", "description"}; materials set them in ernie:thermal:model:params, read with p.get(i), and ernie:thermal:model:data is p.data(i). Built in: "balance" and "diurnal". Raises ValueError for an invalid model or one that fails to compile, with the compiler's diagnostics. backends The names of the render backends. cuda_copy Queues a device-to-device copy between CUDA arrays of the same size on stream . cuda_download A host copy of a CUDA array. cuda_upload A copy of a host array in CUDA memory, for frameworks without CUDA arrays of their own. evict_textures Drops every texture the materials read, so the next render loads them afresh; with cache , their copies in the texture cache too. has_light_pattern Whether light pattern id is registered, built in or added. map_overlay Maps array array ("points", "ends", "values", "colors", "sizes", "worlds"...) of batch batch of overlay overlay for writing in place on the GPU, without copies: a CUDA array over the renderer's own memory for it, holding its values, which the batch now holds. Write into it on stream (which first waits for frames already submitted); the next frames draw it. The batch must have been drawn once. Map again every step (the same memory, no copy), so the stream waits for the frames still reading it. pick_overlay The overlay item the viewer's last frame drew at pixel ( x , y ) (an OverlayHit ), or None. Waits for the device, so for clicks rather than every frame. prim_path The prim path of a PrimId render var value; the empty path for 0 (background) or an unknown id. render Renders scene as the RenderSettings prim settings (or the first one) describes and returns the LdrColor render var: a read-only uint8 array (rows, cols, 4). With device="cuda" the array stays in GPU memory shared with Vulkan, for torch.from_dlpack and friends; it keeps the renderer alive. reset_time Sets the sensor clock to time seconds; the next frame starts there. step step_async(...).wait().fetch(): the outputs by render product path, each with .frames[0].render_vars by RenderVar path. step_async Moves the sensor clock ( time ) on by delta_time seconds, then renders the RenderProduct prims render_products (or the settings' products, or a default one) over the clock since the last frame and returns an Operation at once. sync Uploads the parts of the scene that changed since the last sync. take_validation_messages Vulkan validation messages since the last call. wait_for_textures Syncs scene and waits up to timeout seconds (none: as long as it takes) for the textures its materials read to load in the background, for a program that renders only once none is missing; returns what is still loading or failed. Built in: "balance" and "diurnal". docs.text: Prim types The typed prim classes and the registry they are built from: one class per registered prim type, with a property per attribute. The classes are also exported from ernie itself ( ernie.SphereLight ). Registry and loading Schema Schema(prim: Prim) Base of the typed prim classes: a Prim of the class's registered type or one derived from it. Methods: Name Description __eq__ __getattr__ __hash__ __repr__ __setattr__ at The existing prim at path in a Scene, or at path attributes Every attribute of the type, its root base's first. get read set Sets attributes by Python name, and the transform from set_xform write write_rows Writes row i of each array, by Python name, as that Attributes: __slots__ – define ( _Define [ _SchemaDefine ] ) – path ( Path ) – prim ( Prim ) – prim_type ( PrimType ) – type ( str ) – __slots__ class-attribute instance-attribute __slots__ = ('prim',) define class-attribute instance-attribute define: _Define[_SchemaDefine] = _Define() path property path: Path prim instance-attribute prim: Prim prim_type class-attribute prim_type: PrimType type property type: str __eq__ __eq__(other: object) -> bool __getattr__ __getattr__(name: str) -> Any __hash__ __hash__() -> int __repr__ __repr__() -> str __setattr__ __setattr__(name: str, value: Any) -> None at classmethod at(parent: Scene | Prim | Schema, path: str | Path) -> Self The existing prim at path in a Scene, or at path relative to a prim ("Surface", "Rig/Arm"), as this class. Raises: LookupError – There is no prim there. TypeError – The prim is not of this class's type or one derived from it. attributes classmethod attributes() -> list[AttributeDef] Every attribute of the type, its root base's first. get get(attribute: str, default: Any = None) -> Any read read(attribute: str) -> Any set set(*attribute: Any, time: float | None = None, **attributes: Any) -> Self Sets attributes by Python name, and the transform from translate , rotate , rotation_order , orient and scale ; set(token, value) sets one by USD name. With time , sets their time samples at that time code instead (Scene.set), arrays as Scene.write's. Returns this prim. set_xform set_xform( *, translate: Any = None, rotate: Any = None, rotation_order: str = "XYZ", orient: Any = None, scale: Any = None, ) -> Prim write write(attribute: str, array: Any) -> Prim write_rows classmethod write_rows(scene: Scene, prims: Any, *, stream: Any = None, **arrays: Any) -> None Writes row i of each array, by Python name, as that attribute of prim i of prims (a PrimSet, or a list of paths), every step of a simulation: ernie.PointInstancer.write_rows(scene, prims, positions=p, orientations=q) . translate , orient (x, y, z, w) and scale write the transform ops, which from CUDA arrays pose the prims on the GPU. The arrays are DLPack arrays written without copying; stream is as for Scene.write . Raises: TypeError – A name is not an array attribute of this class or a transform op. typed typed(prim: Prim | Schema) -> Schema | Prim prim as an instance of its type's class, the most derived (a SphereLight's ernie.SphereLight , a Light given as ernie.Light ), or the Prim itself when its type has no class (untyped, or not registered). load_scene load_scene( description: dict[str, Any] | str | PathLike[str], scene: Scene | None = None ) -> Scene Builds prims from a description, into scene or a new Scene, and returns the scene. The description is a dict (or JSON text, or the path of a .json file) from prim paths to prims; each prim is a dict whose "type" names its type (none for an untyped prim, or to leave an existing prim's type alone), whose dict values are its children by name, and whose other values are its attributes, by Python name ( radius ) or USD name ( "inputs:radius" ), with translate , rotate , rotation_order , orient and scale setting its transform ops ( orient a Quat or [w, x, y, z]) and transform a 4 x 4 matrix (rows of four); C++ reads the same format ( ernie/scene/scene_json.h ):: ernie.load_scene({ "/World": {"type": "Xform", "Rock": {"type": "Sphere", "radius": 0.5, "translate": [0, 0, 1]}, "Sun": {"type": "DistantLight", "angle": 0.53}}, "/Render/Settings": {"type": "RenderSettings", "resolution": [640, 480]}, }) C++ loads it ( LoadScene ), so both read a description the same way: each value is read as its attribute's declared kind, checked as setting it is. Lists for array attributes become arrays: int32 for those of whole numbers ( face_vertex_indices , proto_indices ; AttributeDef.is_integer ), float32 for the rest ( points , heights ), whatever the numbers look like; nested lists for one that takes an array in place of its value ( AttributeDef.takes_array : per-vertex display_color ) are a float32 array. A dict may hold Quat s, Path s and prims too, and arrays (NumPy, or any DLPack array, a CUDA one included): where an array goes, written as it is, shared and not copied, its dtype kept, as Scene.write writes one; elsewhere ( translate , a radius ) read as the numbers it holds, which needs a CPU array. Raises: ValueError – A value its attribute does not take, or JSON that does not parse, naming the prim and key (or the line and column). docs.text: load_scene( description: dict[str, Any] | str | PathLike[str], scene: Scene | None = None ) -> Scene Builds prims from a description, into scene or a new Scene, and returns the scene. The description is a dict (or JSON text, or the path of a .json file) from prim paths to prims; each prim is a dict whose "type" names its type (none for an untyped prim, or to leave an existing prim's type alone), whose dict values are its children by name, and whose other values are its attributes, by Python name ( radius ) or USD name ( "inputs:radius" ), with translate , rotate , rotation_order , orient and scale setting its transform ops ( orient a Quat or [w, x, y, z]) and transform a 4 x 4 matrix (rows of four); C++ reads the same format ( ernie/scene/scene_json.h ):: ernie.load_scene({ "/World": {"type": "Xform", "Rock": {"type": "Sphere", "radius": 0.5, "translate": [0, 0, 1]}, "Sun": {"type": "DistantLight", "angle": 0.53}}, "/Render/Settings": {"type": "RenderSettings", "resolution": [640, 480]}, }) C++ loads it ( LoadScene ), so both read a description the same way: each value is read as its attribute's declared kind, checked as setting it is. Lists for array attributes become arrays: int32 for those of whole numbers ( face_vertex_indices , proto_indices ; AttributeDef.is_integer ), float32 for the rest ( points , heights ), whatever the numbers look like; nested lists for one that takes an array in place of its value ( AttributeDef.takes_array : per-vertex display_color ) are a float32 array. A dict may hold Quat s, Path s and prims too, and arrays (NumPy, or any DLPack array, a CUDA one included): where an array goes, written as it is, shared and not copied, its dtype kept, as Scene.write writes one; elsewhere ( translate , a radius ) read as the numbers it holds, which needs a CPU array. Raises: ValueError – A value its attribute does not take, or JSON that does not parse, naming the prim and key (or the line and column). TypeError – The description is not a dict, JSON text or a file path.
docs.title: load_scene

docs.text: volume_sky_light_steps: int Steps up and down through the volumes for how much of the sky's and the ground's light they let through; 0, all. Default 6. USD name ernie:volumes:skyLightSteps .
docs.title: volume_sky_light_steps

docs.text: volume_steps_per_pixel: float Far off, where a pixel spans more of a volume's steps, at most this many steps per pixel's width, the steps growing with distance; 0 keeps every step a volume's own. Default 2.0. USD name ernie:volumes:stepsPerPixel .
docs.title: volume_steps_per_pixel

docs.text: volume_steps_per_voxel: float Steps through a volume per voxel of its densest field, fewer for speed. Default 1.0. USD name ernie:volumes:stepsPerVoxel .
docs.title: volume_steps_per_voxel

docs.text: volume_temporal: bool March a pixel of each block a frame and reproject the others' last results, about four times faster; a frame whose volumes, materials or lights changed, and pixels whose history does not hold, march in full. Off, for reference images. Default True. USD name ernie:volumes:temporal .
docs.title: volume_temporal

docs.text: volume_temporal_animated: bool Volumes whose grids are written again each frame (field writers, simulations) reproject too, each pixel clamped to what the frame marched about it; off, they march in full each frame. Default True. USD name ernie:volumes:temporalAnimated .
docs.title: volume_temporal_animated

docs.text: volume_temporal_block: int Temporal amortisation's blocks, 2 or 4 pixels across: a pixel of each marched a frame, the others reprojected or, where that fails, the block's marched one's where the geometry behind is as far. 2 is about half as fast, its history up to 4 frames old rather than 16. Default 4. USD name ernie:volumes:temporalBlock .
docs.title: volume_temporal_block

docs.text: volume_thin_optical_depth: float A brick of 8^3 voxels whose densest holds back less than this across it is stepped through as one step, lit once; 0 steps through every brick alike. Default 0.05. USD name ernie:volumes:thinOpticalDepth .
docs.title: volume_thin_optical_depth

docs.text: wireframe: str Triangle edges over shaded surfaces, or on flat unlit ones; a bool is "overlay" or "off". The viewport's toolbar may override it. Default 'off'. USD name ernie:wireframe .
docs.title: wireframe
