docs.text: Type Name enum AttributeKind What an attribute holds, from its declared C++ type. enum Axis The axis a primitive is built around, as UsdGeom's axis token. enum BoundaryInterpolation USD's interpolateBoundary . typedef std::pair< glm::vec3, glm::vec3 > Bounds3 Axis-aligned world bounds, low and high corners. enum BufferMemory Where a buffer lives and how the host reaches it. enum CubeFace The faces of a wide camera's views: forward along the camera's -z, then its +x, -x, +y, -y and +z (back). typedef ComputeArrayView CudaArrayView The view of an image CudaInterop::MapImage returns ( array is a CUarray ). enum std::uint32_t Culling How the rasterizer culls what lies outside a view ( ernie:culling ). enum std::uint8_t DType Element types Ernie exchanges. enum std::uint8_t DeviceKind Where a tensor's memory lives: host memory, or the memory of a CUDA or ROCm (HIP) device. enum std::uint32_t Dirty What changed about a prim, as bit flags; see DirtyOf for which attributes set which bit. enum DomeLightMode How dome lights light the scene ( tokens::kDomeLightMode ), as Omniverse RTX's modes. typedef int ExternalHandle Memory or a semaphore exported for another API, such as CUDA: a POSIX file descriptor, or a Win32 NT handle on Windows. enum FaceVaryingInterpolation USD's faceVaryingLinearInterpolation : where face-varying data (such as texture coordinates) stays linear rather than smoothed. typedef std::function< void(VkCommandBuffer, const FieldWriteTarget &)> FieldWriter Records GPU work writing a DenseField 's values ( FieldWriteTarget ) into a frame's command buffer, such as a simulation's compute dispatches. enum std::uint8_t FilterDomain What a filter works on (sensor.slang's SensorPixel ): each band's radiance ( Spectrum ), the channels' electrons (after QE), their digital numbers (after ADC), linear sRGB (after CIE) or the sRGB-encoded display colour (after exposure). enum std::uint8_t FilterKind How a sensor filter runs in the fused sensor kernel (sensor.slang): typedef std::function< Tensor (std::string_view attribute, const Tensor &device)> GpuOpReader Copies an op's tensor on a GPU ( attribute 's, a prim's row of an array) to the host. typedef std::function< Tensor (const Path &path, std::string_view attribute, const Tensor &device)> HostArrayReader A host copy of array attribute of path , written as device on a GPU: for the few arrays the CPU plans with, such as worlds. enum IesType An IES file's photometry: the axis its angles turn about, in the luminaire's frame (x its length and its 0 degree plane, y its width, z up; it shines down -z). enum ImageEncoding How 8- and 16-bit stored values map to linear values. enum std::uint8_t LensProjection How a lens maps the field angle of a ray to its place in the image. enum std::uint32_t LightType Kinds of LightParams . enum MapDevice Where RenderVarOutput::Map delivers an output. enum std::uint8_t MarkerShape The shape of a marker, drawn at a fixed size in pixels. typedef std::function< void(VkCommandBuffer, const MeshWriteTarget &)> MeshWriter Records GPU work writing a mesh ( MeshWriteTarget ) into a frame's command buffer, such as compute dispatches that build its surface. enum std::uint32_t MinimalMode Minimal shading ( ernie:minimal:mode ), after RTX Minimal: for throughput, a product draws in one forward pass straight into its outputs, without the spectral shading, sensor filters, sky or dome; lit by the first four distant lights, unshadowed, and the scene's ambient light. enum MipFilter How MipChain filters each level. enum std::uint32_t NanoVdbType A NanoVDB grid's value type, as PNANOVDB_GRID_TYPE_* numbers it. enum std::uint32_t Occlusion Whether the rasterizer also culls instances hidden behind others ( ernie:occlusion ), with GPU culling and for views only (not shadow views). typedef std::function< ParticleOptics (double wavelengthNm, std::span< const double >)> OpticsModel Optical properties of one particle or molecule at a wavelength (nm), with the phase function at the given cosines. enum std::uint8_t OverlayBatchKind The kinds of item an OverlayBatch holds many of. enum std::uint8_t OverlayDepth How an overlay item meets the scene's surfaces. enum RasterSampleType How a raster's samples are stored. typedef std::map< Path , RenderProductOutput > RenderProductSetOutputs Outputs of a step by render product path. enum std::uint8_t RotationOrder The axis order of an Euler-angle rotate op: the rotation about the first letter's axis applies first, about fixed (extrinsic) axes. enum std::uint8_t SensorFilter The built-in sensor filters a render product runs in order on its spectral radiance, as Chrono::Sensor's filter lists; the rasterizer fuses a chain into one kernel ( PlanSensor ), so the vars below are written only when held: enum SkinningMethod enum SphereTessellation How a sphere is divided into triangles. enum SubdivisionScheme USD's subdivisionScheme . enum TextureColorSpace How a texture's stored values map to linear ones (UsdUVTexture's sourceColorSpace). enum std::uint32_t TextureFormat How a stored texture's texels are laid out: plain texels, or BC1 to BC7 blocks of 4 x 4 texels, uploaded as they are. enum TextureRole What a texture holds, which decides how it is mipped and stored. enum TextureVirtual Whether a texture is virtual, only the tiles in view resident ( ernie:virtualTexture ). enum TextureWrap How a texture repeats outside [0, 1] along one axis (UsdUVTexture's wrapS and wrapT). enum TriangleSubdivision USD's triangleSubdivisionRule . enum std::uint32_t Wireframe How the rasterizer draws triangle edges ( ernie:wireframe ). enum std::uint32_t WorldShadowFit What a world's own shadow map covers ( ernie:shadows:worldFit ). enum std::uint32_t WorldShadows Which casters shadow a batch of views of several worlds ( ernie:shadows:worlds ).

docs.text: Type Name double AirKingFactor (double wavelengthNm, double co2Fraction=360e-6) The King correction factor (6 + 3 rho) / (6 - 7 rho) of dry air for molecular anisotropy, from Bates's factors for N2 and O2, 1 for Ar and 1.15 for CO2, weighted by volume fraction. OpticsModel AirMolecules (double co2Fraction=360e-6) Molecules of dry air: Rayleigh scattering after Bodhaine et al. double AirRefractivity (double wavelengthNm, double co2Fraction=360e-6) The refractivity n - 1 of dry air at 288.15 K and 101325 Pa with a CO2 volume fraction co2Fraction (e.g. constexpr bool Any ( Dirty bits, Dirty flags) Whether bits has any of flags . std::vector< std::string > AovOutputsOf (std::span< const SensorFilterStep > chain, const SensorFilterRegistry & registry) The AOVs chain 's custom filters write ( SensorFilterModel::outputs ), in slot order. void ApplyBlendShape (std::span< float > points, std::span< const float > offsets, std::span< const int > pointIndices, float weight) Adds weight times offsets (x, y, z each) to the points at pointIndices , or to every point in order without them. VkImageAspectFlags AspectOf (VkFormat format) Aspect of an image format: depth for depth formats, colour otherwise. AtmosphereParams AtmosphereParamsOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, const Path & terrain, const std::optional< glm::dvec3 > & eye=std::nullopt) The Atmosphere at path around the planet Terrain __ terrain (empty for none): with a planet Terrain anchored on the ground the planet is at the Terrain 's translation and has its radius unless ernie:atmosphere:planetRadius sets one; without, it is that radius, else the preset planet's mean radius, centred that far below the Atmosphere 's origin. double AtmospherePresetRadius (std::string_view preset) The mean radius (metres) of an Atmosphere preset's planet, as AtmosphereParamsOf takes it; 0 for an unknown preset. void AuthorIsdCamera ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, const CameraParams & camera) Authors the Camera prim at path (defined if missing) with an ISD camera's geometry and exposure time only, as Python's author_framelet does: camera 's transform, scan (frame or pushbroom), focal length, apertures (the horizontal from the image's aspect) and their offsets, pushbroom line offset, Brown-Conrady distortion, clipping range and exposure time. std::optional< Axis > AxisNamed (std::string_view name) The axis named "X", "Y" or "Z"; none for anything else. TextureData BakeMosaic (std::span< const std::filesystem::path > tiles, std::uint32_t columns, const std::filesystem::path & output, const BakeOptions & options={}) As BakeTexture , for an image too large to hold whole: a mosaic of tiles , 8-bit PNG or JPEG images of one size, columns to a row, rows top to bottom (a global mosaic's tiles, such as Blue Marble's eight 21600 x 21600 ones). TextureData BakeTexture (const std::filesystem::path & input, const std::filesystem::path & output, const BakeOptions & options={}) Bakes the image input into a DDS file output for Ernie's textures: every mip down to 1 x 1, filtered as its role says before compression, stored as options says; what virtual textures need ( ernie:virtualTexture ), and a quarter to an eighth of the memory of uncompressed RGBA8. BandedAtmosphere BandAverage (const AtmosphereModel & atmosphere, const SpectralBands & bands, int phaseAngles=256) Averages atmosphere over bands , sampling each band every 10 nm or less. double BandValue (const SpectralBands & bands, int band, const std::function< double(double)> & spectrum) Band band 's value of spectrum : its average over the band, or in RGB mode ( SpectralBands::rgb ) the band's linear sRGB channel of it relative to the equal-energy white's (a flat spectrum's value in every channel), at least 0. std::vector< const PrimTypeDef * > BaseSchemaTypes () This file's types' registry entries, bases first ( PrimTypes ). void BeginRendering (VkCommandBuffer commands, const RenderingTarget & target) Begins dynamic rendering into target , clearing depth to 1, and sets a viewport flipped so that normalised device y points up (row 0 is y = +1), as in WebGPU and OpenGL. std::vector< float > BlackbodyIrradiance (const SpectralBands & bands, double kelvin, double totalIrradiance) The spectral irradiance of a black body at kelvin scaled so that its integral over all wavelengths is totalIrradiance (W/m^2), averaged over each of bands . double BlackbodySpectralIrradiance (double wavelengthNm, double kelvin, double lux) The spectral irradiance at wavelengthNm (W m^-2 nm^-1) of a black body at kelvin whose illuminance is lux , through the CIE photopic luminous efficiency (683 lm/W times y-bar). glm::dvec3 BodyDirection (double latitudeDeg, double longitudeDeg) The body-fixed unit vector of planetocentric latitude latitudeDeg and east longitude longitudeDeg . Path BoundMaterial (const Scene & scene, const Path & prim) The Material prim bound to prim by material:binding , or the empty path. MeshData BoxMesh (const glm::vec3 & size) A box of edge lengths size (UsdGeomCube is a box of equal edges, default 2). SampleBracket BracketOf (std::span< const TimeSample > samples, double time) std::string BrdfModuleName (const BrdfModel & model) Name under which BrdfModules loads model 's module, e.g. std::vector< ShaderModuleSource > BrdfModules (const BrdfModel & model) Slang modules to compile before a shader that uses model : brdf , then the model's module, named BrdfModuleName(model) . std::string_view BrdfSlang () The shared Slang module brdf : BrdfInput , BrdfParams , IBrdf , PI , phase functions, and the backend-neutral helpers: std::optional< std::filesystem::path > CacheDirectory (const char * variable, std::string_view folder) Where one of Ernie's caches keeps its files between runs: the environment variable variable 's folder (empty or "0" for none), else folder in the user's cache folder ( $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ernie , ~/.cache/ernie , LOCALAPPDATA%\ernie ). CloudNoise CachedCloudNoise () MakeCloudNoise 's, read from Ernie's cache folder ( ERNIE_CLOUD_CACHE , else "clouds" in the user's cache folder), else generated (some seconds) and kept there. CloudTransportTable CachedCloudTransport (const CloudTransportOptions & options={}) The canonical transport for Bouthors et al. std::array< glm::dvec3, 4 > CameraImageCorners (const Scene & scene, const Path & camera, double distance) The corners of the image of the Camera at camera , distance metres in front of it: its frustum's section there, from its focal length and apertures, in the world, top left first as Overlay::Image takes them. CameraParams CameraParamsOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) The camera of the Camera prim at path for an image of width x height : its world transform, and UsdGeomCamera's focalLength , verticalAperture , aperture offsets, clippingRange , exposure , exposure:time , exposure:iso , exposure:fStop and exposure:responsivity , and Ernie's ernie:spectral:* , ernie:lens:* and ernie:sensor:* attributes (see tokens.h ). CameraParams CameraParamsOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height, const glm::dmat4 & transform) As CameraParamsOf , with transform in place of the prim's world transform, such as an estimate for a camera posed on the GPU, whose transform the CPU cannot read. glm::dvec3 CameraRay (const CameraParams & camera, glm::dvec2 pixel) The unit ray, in the camera's frame, of sensor position pixel of camera (pixels from the top left corner, centres at + 0.5): its lens's ray table's, or LensRay of its normalised image coordinates. std::vector< const PrimTypeDef * > CameraSchemaTypes () This file's types' registry entries, bases first ( PrimTypes ). bool CanInterpolate (const Tensor & a, const Tensor & b) Whether Interpolate blends a and b (rather than holding a ). MeshData CapsuleMesh (float radius, float height, Axis axis=Axis::Z, std::uint32_t slices=48, std::uint32_t stacks=24) A cylinder of height with hemispherical caps of radius beyond it, so its total length is height + 2 radius (UsdGeomCapsule, default radius 0.5, height 1). OpticsModel CarbonDioxideMolecules (double co2Fraction) Molecules of a CO2 atmosphere such as Mars's: Rayleigh scattering by CO2 at volume fraction co2Fraction (Owens 1967, Bates 1984), with the remainder (on Mars mostly N2 and Ar, whose refractivities are within 7% of air's) scattering as air. double CarbonDioxideRefractivity (double wavelengthNm) The refractivity n - 1 of CO2 at 288.15 K and 101325 Pa. glm::dmat4 CelestialToLocal (double latitude, double longitude, double julianDate) The rotation from the J2000 equatorial frame (x towards right ascension 0, z the north celestial pole) to a site's local frame with x east, y north and z up (Ernie's terrain convention), at latitude and longitude (degrees, east positive) and Julian date julianDate (UT): a StarField 's transform for the sky over the site. void CheckBatchCameras (const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > cameras, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) Checks that cameras can render as one batch: the same projection and spectral bands. std::vector< SensorFilter > CheckFilterChain (std::span< const SensorFilter > chain) chain with Lens prepended when it does not start with it. std::vector< SensorFilterStep > CheckFilterChain (std::span< const SensorFilterStep > chain, const SensorFilterRegistry & registry) chain with the lens prepended when it does not start with it, its custom filters looked up in registry . void CheckRasterView (const RasterView & view, const std::string & what, std::size_t minSide) Throws std::invalid_argument , naming what , unless view has data, at least minSide cells along each side, a row stride of at least its width, and a finite origin and positive finite cell size. void CheckVk (VkResult result, const char * what) Throws std::runtime_error naming what and the result unless result is VK_SUCCESS . double CieDaylight (double wavelengthNm, double kelvin) The relative spectral power of CIE standard illuminant D (daylight) at correlated colour temperature kelvin (4000 to 25000 K; D65 is 6504 K), normalised to 100 at 560 nm, linearly interpolated from the CIE's 10 nm basis functions over 300 to 830 nm and 0 outside. std::vector< glm::dvec3 > CieWeights (const SpectralBands & bands) The colour matching functions averaged over each band, scaled by the band width, so that summing them times band values integrates a spectrum: XYZ = sum_i value_i * weights_i. glm::dvec3 CieXyz (double wavelengthNm) The CIE 1931 2-degree colour matching functions x, y and z at a wavelength, from the multi-lobe Gaussian fit of Wyman, Sloan and Shirley (2013); y peaks at 1 near 555 nm. void CloseExternalHandle ( ExternalHandle handle) Closes an exported handle its importer did not take: a file descriptor an import failed with, or any Win32 handle (CUDA imports them without taking ownership). std::size_t CloudOrderSet (std::size_t order) The order set of light scattered order times (2 or more). double ColorIndexToTemperature (double colorIndex) A star's effective temperature in kelvin from its B-V colour index, by Ballesteros' formula for a black body seen through the Johnson B and V filters (good to a few percent for main sequence stars from about 3000 to 30000 K). std::optional< ColorPrimvar > ColorPrimvarOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & material) That of the Material __ material 's UsdPreviewSurface, if it reads one. std::vector< glm::dvec3 > ColourWeights (const SpectralBands & bands) The weights a renderer turns band values into CIE XYZ with: CieWeights for 16 bands or more; for fewer, weights fitted by least squares so that reflectances upsampled from linear sRGB ( RgbToSigmoid ) and sampled at the band centres, as shaders do, give the XYZ their whole spectra have under the equal-energy illuminant, greys exactly. glm::dmat4 ComposeXformOps (const Scene & scene, const Path & path) The local transform of the prim at path from its transform ops ( Scene::LocalTransform ): the product of the ops xformOpOrder lists, or xformOp:transform without an order. glm::dmat4 ComposeXformOps (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, const GpuOpReader * read) ComposeXformOps reading ops on a GPU through read (none throws, as above): for the few prims the CPU needs posed under prims posed on the GPU, such as lights. void ComputeBarrier (VkCommandBuffer commands) A barrier between compute dispatches recorded into commands : the earlier ones' shader writes before the later ones' shader reads and writes. MeshData ConeMesh (float radius, float height, Axis axis=Axis::Z, std::uint32_t slices=48) A capped cone of total height along axis with its apex at +height / 2 (UsdGeomCone, default radius 1, height 2). void Connect ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view input, const Path & source, std::string_view output) Connects input input of the prim at path to output output of the prim at source . std::unique_ptr< RenderDelegate > CreateRenderDelegate (std::string_view backend, const VulkanContext & context, VkFormat presentFormat=VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM, BrdfRegistry brdfs= BrdfRegistry::WithBuiltins ()) A delegate of backend on context , drawing Record 's LdrColor into colour attachments of presentFormat , with the reflectance models in brdfs . glm::dmat3 CubeFaceAxes ( CubeFace face) Face face 's axes in the camera's frame (columns x, y, z): a camera on them looks down their -z, as the camera itself does on the front face. double CubeFaceExtent (double facePixels, double marginPixels=2.0) The tangent of the half field a face's view covers: 1 (45 degrees) plus marginPixels of a face facePixels across, so bilinear taps at a seam stay inside the face they sample. CubeFace CubeFaceOf (const glm::dvec3 & ray, int faces= kCubeFaces ) The face, of the first faces ( kCubeFaces or kAllCubeFaces ), whose view direction lies nearest unit ray ray (in the camera's frame): the largest of -z, x, -x, y, -y and, with the back face, z. glm::dvec2 CubeFacePlane ( CubeFace face, const glm::dvec3 & ray) Where ray crosses face face 's image plane at unit distance: its tangent-plane coordinates (x right, y up on the face), in [-1, 1] across the face's 90 degrees. glm::dvec3 CubeFaceRay ( CubeFace face, glm::dvec2 plane) The unit ray through face face 's tangent-plane coordinates plane . int CubeFacesOf (const CameraParams & camera) How many cube faces camera 's views render on: 1 when it needs none ( NeedsCubeFaces ), the first five ( kCubeFaces ) while its field stays within kFiveFacesAngle (less a degree, for the faces' bilinear taps), else all six. Culling CullingOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings) The culling of the RenderSettings prim settings ( ernie:culling ), Culling::Gpu when unset. MeshData CylinderMesh (float radius, float height, Axis axis=Axis::Z, std::uint32_t slices=48) A capped cylinder of total height along axis (UsdGeomCylinder, default radius 1, height 2). constexpr DType DTypeOf () The DType of a C++ element type. constexpr DType DTypeOf< double > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< float > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< std::int32_t > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< std::int64_t > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< std::uint16_t > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< std::uint32_t > () constexpr DType DTypeOf< std::uint8_t > () TextureData DecodeBlocks (const TextureData & texture) texture with its BC blocks decoded, for devices that cannot sample them: to the same channels, 8 bits each (BC1, BC3 and BC7 to RGBA8, sRGB where they were; BC4 to R8; BC5 to RG8), every layer and mip. float DecodeSlopeDeviation (float encoded) std::vector< SensorFilter > DefaultFilterChain () Every filter in its natural order: the sensor chain then the photographic chain. std::uint32_t DefaultSphereLevel ( SphereTessellation tessellation) The level TessellatedSphere uses for 0: some 2,000 to 5,000 triangles each (24 stacks, 4 subdivisions, 16 quads a face edge, N_side 16). std::vector< std::uint8_t > DenseNanoVdbGrid (std::span< const float > values, const glm::ivec3 & shape, double voxelSize, const glm::dvec3 & origin, std::string_view name="") A NanoVDB float grid (a fog volume) of dense values , shape x by y by z with z fastest (a C-order (x, y, z) array), active where not 0: as NanoVDB keeps a grid in memory, for a NanoVDBField 's array. std::vector< std::uint8_t > DenseNanoVdbTopology (const glm::ivec3 & shape, double voxelSize, const glm::dvec3 & origin, std::string_view name, DenseNanoVdbLayout & layout) As DenseNanoVdbGrid , with every voxel of shape active and 0, for values written into it in place later, such as by the GPU each step of a simulation (a DenseField on a device); layout says where they go. Dirty DirtyOf (std::string_view attribute) The dirty bit that setting or writing attribute raises: Transform for xformOps, else what the registered types declare for it ( AttributeMeta::dirty , such as Points for points ), else Primvars for primvars and Params for anything else. glm::dmat4 DistantLightTransform (glm::dvec3 towardsLight) Transform of a DistantLight shining from towardsLight : its +z axis points along it, so the light travels down -z as UsdLux defines. std::vector< double > DiurnalSurfaceTemperatures (const RegolithProperties & regolith, double latitude, int samples) The surface temperature of level ground at latitude (radians) over a solar day, samples evenly spaced from local midnight, in kelvin, the sun in the equator's plane: the regolith's heat conduction solved implicitly on a grid finer near the surface, run to its periodic state, absorbed sunlight and the geothermal flux in, thermal emission out. DiurnalTable DiurnalTemperatureTable (const RegolithProperties & regolith, int latitudes, int times, std::vector< float > inertias={}, std::vector< float > albedos={}) DiurnalSurfaceTemperatures at latitudes latitudes from 0 to 90 degrees and times local times, for each of inertias ( WithThermalInertia ; none, the regolith's own) and albedos (none, the regolith's own), the rows baked in parallel. std::vector< DomeDirection > DomeDirectionsOf (const Image & map, std::size_t count) count directions standing for latitude-longitude dome map map , for lighting with it as shadowed distant lights: Debevec's median cut, splitting the most energetic region along its longer side (in angle) where half its energy (luminance times solid angle) lies on each side, until there are count . std::array< glm::vec3, 9 > DomeIrradianceSh (const Tensor & latlong, const glm::dmat3 & rotation) Diffuse irradiance over pi of a latitude-longitude RGB map ( tokens::kLightTexture layout) turned by rotation into the world, as order-2 spherical harmonics (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan 2001): the map's projection weighted by each texel's exact solid angle, convolved with the clamped cosine. std::optional< Image > DomeMapOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path) The DomeLight at path 's map ( tokens::kLightTexture ) as a linear RGB image for drawing behind the scene; none without one. DomeParams DomeParamsOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, const SpectralBands & bands) The DomeLight at path for bands : radiance ernie:spectrum (W m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1), or in relative units inputs:intensity times 2^ inputs:exposure as luminance (cd/m^2) with the shape of inputs:color and the enabled colour temperature; its map ernie:texture (uniform without one) rotated by its transform. DropletPhaseTable DropletPhase (double effectiveRadiusUm, double spread, const SpectralBands & bands, std::size_t angles=1024) The phase function of water droplets of effective radius effectiveRadiusUm (micrometres) in a gamma distribution of width spread (its gamma: effective variance 1 / (spread + 2)), at each band's centre, sampled at angles angles. AtmosphereModel EarthAtmosphere (double radius, const EarthAtmosphereOptions & options={}) Earth's atmosphere over a planet of radius radius (m). float EncodeSlopeDeviation (float sigma) A slope standard deviation sigma (0 or more) as a value in [0, 1) for 8-bit storage, sigma / (1 + sigma), finest near 0; DecodeSlopeDeviation inverts it. TextureData EncodeTexture (std::span< const Image > mips, TextureFormat format, ImageEncoding encoding, int quality=1, BlockEncoder * encoder=nullptr) mips (full size first, as MipChain makes them) stored in format , 8-bit values encoded with encoding ; BC blocks over a mip's edge repeat its last row and column; quality is BC7's effort, 0 to 4. glm::dvec3 EqualEnergyXyzToLinearSrgb (glm::dvec3 xyz) Linear sRGB of a colour given in CIE XYZ relative to the equal-energy illuminant E (white at the XYZ of a flat spectrum under the colour matching functions), adapted to sRGB's D65 white with the Bradford transform, so flat spectra map to greys. glm::dvec3 EulerAngles (const glm::dmat3 & rotation, RotationOrder order) Euler angles in degrees (x, y, z) whose EulerRotation in order is rotation , a rotation matrix. glm::dmat3 EulerRotation (glm::dvec3 degrees, RotationOrder order) The rotation of Euler angles degrees (one per axis, as x, y, z, whatever the order) applied in order : for XYZ, Rz * Ry * Rx with column vectors. std::optional< Bounds3 > ExtentOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & prim) The prim's extent : six numbers, low then high corner, as a float array value or a CPU array; none if unset or malformed. std::optional< DomeSunExtraction > ExtractDomeSun (const Image & map) The sun of dome map map , if it has one: the brightest texel's connected region of texels above kDomeSunThreshold of its luminance, when that region is compact (under 5 degrees across), much brighter than the sky (its peak over 20 times the map's median luminance) and carries at least 5% of the map's irradiance. JointDualQuaternion FactorJoint (const glm::mat4 & transform) transform factored for dual quaternion skinning: its rotation the orthonormal polar factor of its 3 by 3, the rest its scale. std::string FieldRelationship (std::string_view name) The relationship naming a Volume 's field name : "field:<name>". const NanoVdbGrid * FindNanoVdbGrid (std::span< const NanoVdbGrid > grids, std::string_view name, int index=0) The grid UsdVol's OpenVDBAsset names: the index th grid (0 the first) named name , or the index th grid of the file when name is empty; nullptr if there is none. const PrimTypeDef * FindPrimType (std::string_view name) The registered prim type named name , or null. const MeasuredReflectance * FindReflectance (std::string_view id) The measured reflectance with id id , or null. const AttributeDef * FindXformOp (std::string_view attribute) The transform op attribute names ("xformOp:orient", "xformOp:translate:pivot") as a declared attribute, any prim's: xformOp:translate and the Euler rotations a Vec3 , xformOp:scale a Vec3 or one number, rotateX (Y, Z) a Double in degrees, xformOp:orient a Quat and xformOp:transform a Matrix , each also taking an array of them, a pose per prim ( AttributeMeta::array ); null for other names and ops Ernie does not know. std::optional< std::uint64_t > FrameOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings) The frame number the RenderSettings prim settings authors in ernie:frame , if it does: the frame an image's noise and samples derive from ( FrameSeed ), so a simulation can render any frame again without the ones before it. FrameParams FrameParamsOf (const Scene & scene, const RenderPrims & prims, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) The frame parameters for prims of scene , for an image of width x height : constexpr std::uint32_t FrameSeed (std::uint32_t seed, std::uint32_t stream, std::uint64_t frame) The seed of frame frame of stream stream under the authored seed , from which a frame's temporal noise and samples derive. MaterialXShader GenerateMaterialXShader (const MaterialXSource & source) Generates source 's element's shading for Ernie. glm::dvec3 GeodeticNormal (const glm::dvec3 & surface, const glm::dvec3 & radii) The ellipsoid's outward unit normal at its point surface : parallel to surface_i / radii_i^2. glm::dvec3 GeodeticSurfacePoint (const glm::dvec3 & point, const glm::dvec3 & radii) The point of the ellipsoid of semi-axes radii (along x, y and z, centred at the origin) whose normal passes through point : the foot of the geodetic normal, where a point at that place's height stands. std::vector< const PrimTypeDef * > GeometrySchemaTypes () This file's types' registry entries, bases first ( PrimTypes ). bool GetBool (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, bool fallback) The attribute as a bool (from a bool or an int), or fallback . std::optional< Connection > GetConnection (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view input) The connection of input input (e.g. std::optional< std::vector< float > > GetFloats (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute) The attribute as a list of numbers, or nullopt if it is unset or not numeric: a float array, or a 2-, 3- or 4-vector ( vec , dvec or ivec ), which is how short lists arrive from bindings such as Python's (a list of four numbers is a vec4 ), or a single number. double GetNumber (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, double fallback) The attribute as a number, or fallback if it is unset or not numeric. const PrimTypeDef & GetPrimType (std::string_view name) The registered prim type named name . bool GetRow (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, std::span< double > numbers) Fills numbers from the attribute's array on the CPU when it holds exactly that many (float32, float64 or int32), as a column's row does ( Column ); false otherwise. Path GetTarget (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute) The attribute as a relationship target, or the empty path. std::string GetToken (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, std::string_view fallback) The attribute as a token or string, or fallback . glm::dvec2 GetVec2 (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, glm::dvec2 fallback) The attribute as a 2-vector (from vec2 , dvec2 or ivec2 ), or fallback . glm::dvec3 GetVec3 (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, glm::dvec3 fallback) The attribute as a 3-vector (from vec3 or dvec3 ), or fallback . const Tensor * GpuPosesOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & camera) camera 's poses ( tokens::kPoses ) if they stay on the GPU ( tokens::kPosesDevice ): a contiguous float32 CUDA array of (views, 4, 4), (views, 16) or (views, 7), and "gpu" (the default). std::optional< Path > GpuXformAnchorOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path) The nearest prim from path up whose pose is on the GPU ( GpuXformOf ) and whose transform reaches path (no !resetXformStack! between), or none. std::optional< GpuXform > GpuXformOf (const Scene & scene, const Path & path, bool host=false) The prim's GPU pose, or none when none of its transform ops is a GPU array. double GreenwichMeanSiderealTime (double julianDate) The Greenwich mean sidereal time in degrees [0, 360) at Julian date julianDate (UT). const RefractiveIndex & HematiteRefractiveIndex () The refractive index of hematite (alpha-Fe2O3) over 220-1000 nm, as tabulated by CosmoScout VR (CC0) after Ehlers et al., used with feldspar for Martian dust. std::size_t ImageBytes ( TextureFormat format, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) Bytes of a width x height image of format : whole blocks. Image ImageOfTensor (const Tensor & tensor, ImageEncoding encoding) A detail texture tensor as an Image : float32 values are linear; uint8 values are sRGB-encoded when encoding is Srgb and linear otherwise. docs.text: Spectral quantities for Ernie's spectral rendering: wavelengths in nanometres, spectral irradiance in W m^-2 nm^-1 and spectral radiance in W m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1. The Sun's light above any atmosphere. Light scattering by molecules and particles, for participating media such as atmospheres: Rayleigh scattering by gases, Mie scattering by spheres and particle size distributions, and tabulated absorption cross sections. Airless bodies' diurnal surface temperatures from a 1-D model of their regolith. A planet's atmosphere as constituents (gases, aerosols, absorbers) with physical optical properties and vertical density profiles, and its reduction to a camera's spectral bands. Skeletal skinning and blend shapes on the CPU, as UsdSkel defines them: the reference the GPU's skinning is checked against. Skinned meshes resolved from the scene as UsdSkel defines them, in two parts: a mesh's binding to its skeleton, which changes rarely ( SkinBindingOf ), and its pose at a time ( SkinPoseOf ), from its skeleton's ( SkeletonPoseOf , shared by the skeleton's meshes). Deterministic random streams shared by every render backend. How every render delegate reads a Scene : which prims a render uses, its render products, and the camera, lights, materials, meshes and instances as plain data, so backends differ only in how they draw. MaterialX materials: a Material 's MaterialX surface (a network of Shader prims of MaterialX node definitions on outputs:mtlx:surface, or a material of a .mtlx document it names) as a MaterialX document, and the Slang that MaterialX's shader generation writes for it. Rays of a lens in the camera's frame, and the cube faces a wide camera's views are rendered on, for fields the single pinhole raster image cannot take (its tangent grows without bound towards 90 degrees off axis). Time samples: an attribute's values at time codes, and its value at any time between them, as USD interpolates them ( UsdAttribute with linear interpolation, the stage default). Helpers for authoring and reading the schemas in tokens.h . Scenes described in JSON, the format of Python's ernie.load_scene : Prim types as reflected schemas: each type declares its attributes once, as a list of (C++ type, name, USD token, fallback, metadata) entries, and that list gives both a typed view class over Scene ( GetRadius , HasRadius , SetRadius ) and the type's entry in a runtime registry ( PrimTypeDef ), which generic code walks: Python's typed prim classes, the viewer's property panels, loaders. References: * NASA Planetary Data System, "Planetary Data System Standards Reference", version 3.8, 2009: chapter 12 (the object description language of PDS3 labels). * G. A. Neumann, "Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter Reduced Data Record and Derived Products Software Interface Specification", version 2.42, 2010 (the LDEM products, their labels and simple cylindrical grids). * J. P. Snyder, "Map Projections: A Working Manual", USGS Professional Paper 1395, 1987 (the equirectangular projection; the polar stereographic, eq. 21-33 and 21-34).The view reads and writes the scene's attributes by their USD names, so it changes nothing about storage or change tracking; unset attributes read as the declared fallback, the one place Ernie keeps it. A schema's header declares its attributes with an X-macro list and its class with ERNIE_SCHEMA_BODY ; its source defines the registry entry with ERNIE_DEFINE_SCHEMA , and prim_type.cpp lists it in the registry. See light_schemas.h . References: * Blender, Cycles' node types and sockets ( NODE_DEFINE , SOCKET_* , NODE_SOCKET_API ), https://projects.blender.org/blender/cycles/src/branch/main/src/graph/node_type.h * Pixar, UsdLux and generated schema classes, https://openusd.org/release/api/usd_lux_page_front.html The top level maps prim paths (absolute, or relative to the root) to prims; "/" holds the stage metadata ( Stage ), as {"/": {"upAxis": "Z", "timeCodesPerSecond": 60}} . A prim is an object: "type" names its type ( Scene::Define ; registered or not). Without one, a new prim is untyped and an existing prim keeps its type and attributes. Keys whose values are objects are its children, by name; the other keys are its attributes, by the Python name of one its type declares ( AttributeDef::pyName , "cell_size") or by USD name ("inputs:intensity"). translate (3 numbers), rotate (3 Euler angles in degrees), rotation_order ("XYZ", ..., "ZYX"), orient (a quaternion as [w, x, y, z], the real part first as USD writes one and as Python's Quat(w, x, y, z) takes it) and scale (one number or 3) set its transform ops ( SetXform ); transform sets xformOp:transform to a 4 x 4 matrix given as 4 rows of 4 numbers (math convention: column vectors, translation in the last column). Values convert as Python's do: booleans, integers (32-bit), other numbers as doubles, strings, arrays of strings, arrays of 2 numbers ( ivec2 when both are integers), 3 or 4 as vectors, other lengths as float arrays, and 4 x 4 nested arrays as matrices; nested arrays other than 4 x 4 are a float32 tensor. Those are the rules for undeclared attributes only. A declared one, or a transform op ( FindXformOp : xformOp:orient:<suffix> too), is read as its kind: a tensor ( points , heights ) as a CPU tensor, int32 for one of whole numbers ( AttributeMeta::integer : indices, counts) and float32 for any other, whatever the numbers look like, written with Scene::Write ; an AttributeMeta::array attribute's array of values, nested deeper than one value (a per-vertex primvars:displayColor , N rows of 3), as a float32 tensor; a Vec4 's 4 numbers as doubles, a Quat 's as [w, x, y, z] and a Matrix as 4 rows; then converted to its type ( AttributeDef::Coerce : a string to a relationship target, say), a AttributeMeta::lenient attribute keeping a value its type cannot convert. Values are checked as Scene::Set checks them ( Validate ). SaveScene writes the format back, so that LoadScene of its text into an empty scene rebuilds the scene: every prim but the viewer's (under tokens::kSessionRoot ), roots by path at the top level and the others nested as children by name, "type" first when typed, then the attributes by USD name in name order (transform ops as xformOp:* and xformOpOrder attributes, not the translate -style keys), then the children in path order. Values are written as LoadScene reads them back: Path s and lists of them as strings, matrices as 4 rows, quaternions as [w, x, y, z], floats in their shortest form that reads back as the same float, and tensors as arrays nested by their shape. Limits: * large tensors make large files (a number per element, a line per row), and NaN or infinite numbers cannot be written (JSON has none); * declared attributes come back as their declared types; undeclared ones as LoadScene reads the JSON: Path s as strings, 2 to 4 numbers as vectors (a float array or a rank-1 tensor of that length among them, and a dvec4 or a quaternion off xformOp:orient as a float vec4 ), other rank-1 arrays as float arrays, nested arrays as float32 tensors (any element type), and a 4 x 4 tensor as a matrix; * declared tensors come back int32 ( AttributeMeta::integer ) or float32 whatever their element type; an empty tensor comes back without its shape and a rank-0 one with shape [1]; * an empty list of strings or paths comes back as an empty float array (declared relationship lists convert it back), and unset ( Value::Empty ) values are left out; * overlays ( Scene::GetOverlay ) are not prims and are not written; * GPU tensors are not copied to the host: SaveScene throws for them. The readers accept any numeric type an author might use for an attribute (an int , float or double number; a vec or dvec vector), since bindings such as Python's produce doubles. Reference: Pixar, "UsdAttribute: Interpolation of Time Samples", https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_attribute.html The camera's frame is USD's: x right, y up, looking down -z. A cube face is a square pinhole view of 90 degrees (plus a margin) along one of the camera's axes; the sensor follows each pixel's lens ray to the face it leaves through. kernel/film/cube_faces.slang holds the same conventions for the sensor kernel. References: * N. Greene, "Environment Mapping and Other Applications of World Projections", IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications 6(11):21-29, 1986 (cube maps). * Khronos, "Vulkan Specification", 16.5.4 "Cube Map Face Selection" (selection by the largest-magnitude component).MaterialX itself stays inside Ernie: only plain types cross. References: * Academy Software Foundation, "MaterialX Specification" 1.39, https://materialx.org/Specification.html * Academy Software Foundation, MaterialX 1.39.5: MaterialXGenSlang. Every random decision a renderer makes (sensor noise, and the samples of ray and path tracers) derives from three numbers: a seed the scene authors, a stream naming what is rendered (a render product, StreamOf its path) and the frame number. The same scene, settings and frame then render the same image on any machine, in any order, whatever else renders alongside. Reference: M. Jarzynski and M. Olano, "Hash Functions for GPU Rendering", Journal of Computer Graphics Techniques 9(3):21-38, 2020 (pcg3d). Skinning on the CPU ( SkinnedPoints ) and on the GPU both take them. Matrices are column-vector (glm) ones. References: Pixar, UsdSkel, https://openusd.org/release/api/_usd_skel__intro.html and pxr/usd/usdSkel/utils.cpp (UsdSkelSkinPointsLBS, ...DQS). N. Magnenat-Thalmann, R. Laperrière, D. Thalmann, "Joint-dependent local deformations for hand animation and object grasping", Graphics Interface '88, 26-33, 1988. https://doi.org/10.20380/GI1988.04 L. Kavan, S. Collins, J. Žára, C. O'Sullivan, "Geometric Skinning with Approximate Dual Quaternion Blending", ACM TOG 27(4), 105, 2008. https://doi.org/10.1145/1409625.1409627 Altitudes and radii are in metres, number densities in m^-3, cross sections in m^2 and coefficients in m^-1. Wavelengths are in nanometres in vacuum, radii in metres and cross sections in m^2. Phase functions are in sr^-1, normalised to integrate to 1 over the sphere, and take the cosine of the scattering angle (1 is forward).

docs.text: The Atmosphere at path around the planet Terrain __ terrain (empty for none): with a planet Terrain anchored on the ground the planet is at the Terrain 's translation and has its radius unless ernie:atmosphere:planetRadius sets one; without, it is that radius, else the preset planet's mean radius, centred that far below the Atmosphere 's origin. AtmosphereParams ernie::AtmosphereParamsOf ( const Scene & scene, const Path & path, const Path & terrain, const std::optional< glm::dvec3 > & eye=std::nullopt ) The air is a spherical shell. On an ellipsoid Terrain ( ernie:radii ) its sphere, of the Atmosphere 's radius or else the preset's, touches the ellipsoid at the foot of the normal through eye (world), sharing its tangent plane there, so the ground and the air's bottom agree under the viewer and the altitude is right (three-geospatial's altitude correction); without an eye, it is centred on the Terrain . docs.text: As BakeTexture , for an image too large to hold whole: a mosaic of tiles , 8-bit PNG or JPEG images of one size, columns to a row, rows top to bottom (a global mosaic's tiles, such as Blue Marble's eight 21600 x 21600 ones). TextureData ernie::BakeMosaic ( std::span< const std::filesystem::path > tiles, std::uint32_t columns, const std::filesystem::path & output, const BakeOptions & options={} ) Each tile is read and its top mips encoded into the file in turn, as far as they halve exactly and split into whole blocks at the tiles' edges; the smaller mips come from those tiles' last mips joined. So at most two tiles' texels (one decoding as the other encodes) and the joined mips are held. Normal maps are not baked as mosaics. Returns the stored texture's layout, its texels in the file only. Exception: std::invalid_argument for tiles that are not whole rows or not of one size, or normal maps; std::runtime_error if a tile cannot be read or the output written.

docs.text: Bakes the image input into a DDS file output for Ernie's textures: every mip down to 1 x 1, filtered as its role says before compression, stored as options says; what virtual textures need ( ernie:virtualTexture ), and a quarter to an eighth of the memory of uncompressed RGBA8. TextureData ernie::BakeTexture ( const std::filesystem::path & input, const std::filesystem::path & output, const BakeOptions & options={} ) Returns the stored texture. 8-bit PNG and JPEG colour and data bake in 8 bits, each mip made from the last and dropped once encoded (about 4 bytes a texel of the image beyond the output); normal maps, EXR and 16-bit images through floats (16 bytes a texel for every mip). TIFF, PDS3 and .mosaic colour and data bake a band at a time ( RasterBake ), the stored texture returned mapped from output . References: * R. Geldreich, "bc7enc_rdo" (bc7enc and rgbcx). https://github.com/richgel999/bc7enc_rdo Exception: std::runtime_error if the input cannot be read or the output written; std::invalid_argument as EncodeTexture .

docs.text: Imports the USD file file (.usd, .usda, .usdc or .usdz) into scene at root : OpenUSD composes the stage (sublayers, references, payloads, inherits, variants), then each prim becomes the Ernie prim of the same name and type. UsdImportResult ernie::ImportUsd ( Scene & scene, const Path & root, const std::filesystem::path & file, const UsdImportOptions & options={} ) The file's default prim becomes root itself, as a USD reference to the file would place it; without one, its root prims go under root , an Xform . The root's transform converts the file's upAxis and metersPerUnit into the scene's. Translated: Xform and Scope , Mesh (welding faceVarying normals into vertices; leftHanded faces reversed), the Cube , Sphere , Cylinder , Cone , Capsule and Plane shapes, Points , PointInstancer , cameras, UsdLux lights, and UsdPreviewSurface materials (bound through ComputeBoundMaterial ), with materials of other render contexts (OmniPBR's MDL, say) approximated by UsdPreviewSurface. Instances are expanded. UsdSkel skeletons, their animations sampled at each time code, blend shapes and meshes' bindings become Ernie's own ( skel_schemas.h ), the meshes at rest for the renderer to pose. Other prim types become Xforms, with a warning. OpenUSD lives in a plugin, libernie_usd , loaded on first use: the one beside Ernie's library or Python module, or the one the environment variable ERNIE_USD_PLUGIN names. Exception: std::runtime_error if the plugin is missing or cannot load (another OpenUSD already in the process, say), or if the file cannot be opened.

docs.text: Reads a DDS or KTX2 file as stored ( TextureData ), by extension: mapped into memory and read in place ( TextureData::mapping ), so its texels come from disk only as they are used, a virtual texture's tiles in view rather than the whole file; supercompressed KTX2 levels are decoded into memory. TextureData ernie::LoadTextureFile ( const std::filesystem::path & path ) DDS: the DX10 header's DXGI formats, the legacy DXT1 to DXT5, ATI1, ATI2, BC4U/S and BC5U/S codes, and 32-bit RGBA or BGRA masks; 2D textures, arrays and cube maps, not volumes. KTX2: the formats above by their VkFormat, stored or zstd-supercompressed; and Basis Universal's ETC1S (BasisLZ) and UASTC, transcoded to BC blocks: BC5 for two channels (a normal map's x and y, labelled ETC1S RRR and GGG or UASTC RRRG or RG, as toktx --normal_mode writes them), BC6H for HDR and BC7 otherwise. References: * Microsoft, "DDS programming guide" (DDS_HEADER, DDS_HEADER_DXT10). https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddds/dx-graphics-dds-pguide * Khronos, "KTX File Format Specification", version 2.0. https://registry.khronos.org/KTX/specs/2.0/ktxspec.v2.html * Binomial, "Basis Universal" (the transcoder). https://github.com/BinomialLLC/basis_universal Exception: std::runtime_error if the file cannot be read, is malformed or truncated, or holds a format or layout it does not read.

docs.text: The standard library of sensor filters, written in Slang like custom ones and registered with every renderer, for a SensorFilter prim's ernie:filter:type : std::vector< SensorFilterModel > ernie::StandardSensorFilters () psf (spatial, spectrum): the lens's point-spread, diffraction for the camera's f-number per band (a Gaussian fit to the Airy disc) and a Gaussian blur in pixels; before qe . defocus (spatial, spectrum): thin-lens depth of field from the camera's fStop and focusDistance ; before qe . bayer (pixel, electrons): a Bayer colour filter mosaic, pattern 0 RGGB, 1 BGGR, 2 GRBG, 3 GBRG; best between noise and adc . demosaic (spatial, digital): interpolates the mosaic back, method 0 bilinear or 1 Malvar-He-Cutler; after adc . AOV mosaic : the mosaic it read. blooming (spatial, electrons): charge beyond the full well spilling along columns, antiBlooming the fraction drained; after qe . AOV overflow : the charge beyond the well. whiteBalance (pixel, rgb): red , green and blue gains; after cie . colorMatrix (pixel, rgb): a 3 x 3 colour correction matrix m00 .. m22 ; after cie . bolometer (integrator, electrons; temporal): an uncooled microbolometer's counts from its in-band signal, with its time constant, NETD noise, residual fixed pattern and drift; and the brightness temperature for an object's emissivity and reflected temperature, the BrightnessTemperature var's; in place of qe . thermalDisplay (integrator, rgb): a thermal camera's picture of the brightness temperature, over a fixed kelvin range or one its automatic gain control takes from the last frame, in a palette (white-hot, black-hot, ironbow, rainbow); in place of cie , after bolometer . compand (pixel, digital): square-root companding from inputBits to outputBits ; after adc . toneCurve (pixel, display): each channel through curve (33 samples over 0 to 1); after exposure . agx (pixel, display): the AgX filmic display transform of the exposed linear colour, exposure stops more, in place of the exposure's clip; after exposure . spectralTransmission (band): each band times curve (48 samples, 360 to 830 nm), a measured filter's transmission; before qe and cie . glare (spatial, rgb; pyramid): a wide power-law halo of scattered light around bright sources in the image; after cie . flare (spatial, electrons; pyramid): lens flare ghosts, the image's bright sources as defocused aperture shapes on the line through the principal point, each at its own scale, size and coating tint; after qe , before noise . strayLight (band): the sun's light from outside the field as a veil over the image, its irradiance times the optics' point source transmittance at its angle off the axis (from the frame's sun, which the image lacks); before qe and cie . lag (pixel, electrons; temporal): a fraction of each frame's charge read out with the next. temporalAverage (pixel, rgb; temporal): an exponential moving average, alpha the new frame's weight. smear (spatial, electrons): a frame-transfer CCD's readout smear ( transferTime ) and reset smear ( resetTime ), on either side of bright sources; before noise . radiation (pixel, electrons): particle hits, flux per cm^2 per second, each a track of charge; before noise . AOV deposited : their electrons. commsErrors (spatial, digital): lost packets, line slips and bit errors of a downlink; after adc . AOV errors : where. gaussianPsf (spatial, electrons; pyramid): scattered light as a weighted sum of Gaussians; before noise . Each file's header cites its references.

docs.text: Checks that attribute may be set on a prim of type (at path , for messages), and that value is of its declared type, or, when null ( Scene::Write ), that it takes an array, as Scene::Set and Scene::Write do: void ernie::Validate ( const PrimTypeDef * type, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, const Value * value ) a declared attribute, or a transform op ( FindXformOp ), takes what its readers take ( AttributeDef::Coerce ; anything for AttributeMeta::lenient ones), and an array only when it is a tensor or AttributeMeta::array (a tensor also takes small arrays as values); an undeclared one is an error when its name has no namespace ( radus ), or is in a namespace the type declares attributes in and does not open ( inputs:radus on a light, ernie:sensor:noize on a camera), with the closest declared names suggested; everything else is allowed: other namespaces (custom data such as user:speed ), the type's open namespaces ( PrimTypeDef::openNamespaces ), undeclared primvars:* , xformOpOrder and ops Ernie does not know, and UsdShade connections ( <input>.connect ). A null type (an untyped prim, or one of a type not registered) checks only what Ernie reads on every prim: transform ops and Imageable 's attributes ( visibility , ernie:world , ernie:quaternionOrder ), any other name being allowed. Exception: std::invalid_argument naming the prim and the attribute.

docs.text: Class ernie::BindlessHeap ClassList > ernie > BindlessHeap Every pass's textures and samplers in one descriptor set (set 1 of every PipelineLayout ), each at an index shaders take from their uniforms: bindless descriptor indexing, so a pass's long-lived textures cost it no binding of its own (bindless.slang declares the arrays). More... #include <ernie/device/bindless.h> Classes Type Name class Slot A slot of the heap, freed when destroyed; move-only. Public Types Type Name enum std::uint32_t Kind The heap's arrays, in bindless.slang's bindings. Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr std::uint32_t kKinds = 5 constexpr std::uint64_t kRetireFrames = 3 Frames a freed slot waits before reuse. constexpr std::uint32_t kSamplers = 256 constexpr std::uint32_t kTextures = 4096 Public Functions Type Name Slot AddImage ( Kind kind, VkImageView view, VkImageLayout layout=VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL) A slot holding view (of Texture2D or Texture2DArray kind), sampled in layout . Slot AddSampler (VkSampler sampler, bool comparison=false) A slot holding sampler , a comparison sampler or not, shared as AddImage 's are: samplers are few ( Sampler s of the same state share one), the materials using them many. void AdvanceFrame () Lets slots freed kRetireFrames frames ago be reused; the renderer calls it once a frame. void Bind (VkCommandBuffer commands, VkPipelineBindPoint point, VkPipelineLayout pipelineLayout) const Binds the heap as set 1 of pipelineLayout . BindlessHeap (const VulkanContext & context) BindlessHeap (const BindlessHeap &) = delete void Forget (std::uint64_t object) Stops sharing the slots of object (an image view or sampler), which is being destroyed, so that a new object given its handle gets a slot of its own; slots still held stay until released. std::uint32_t InUse ( Kind kind) const Slots in use of kind , for tests. VkDescriptorSetLayout Layout () const BindlessHeap & operator= (const BindlessHeap &) = delete ~BindlessHeap () Detailed Description Buffers need none: shaders read them through their addresses ( GpuBuffer::Address ). A slot's descriptor is written when it is added, while the set may be bound (update after bind), and a freed slot is reused only a few frames later ( AdvanceFrame ), or once the device is idle when the heap runs out, so work in flight never sees it change. Reference: Khronos, VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing (core in Vulkan 1.2), https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing.html Public Types Documentation enum Kind The heap's arrays, in bindless.slang's bindings. enum ernie::BindlessHeap::Kind { Texture2D = 0, Texture2DArray = 1, Sampler = 2, ComparisonSampler = 3, UintTexture2DArray = 4 }; Public Static Attributes Documentation variable kKinds constexpr std::uint32_t ernie::BindlessHeap::kKinds; variable kRetireFrames Frames a freed slot waits before reuse. constexpr std::uint64_t ernie::BindlessHeap::kRetireFrames; variable kSamplers constexpr std::uint32_t ernie::BindlessHeap::kSamplers; variable kTextures constexpr std::uint32_t ernie::BindlessHeap::kTextures; Public Functions Documentation function AddImage A slot holding view (of Texture2D or Texture2DArray kind), sampled in layout . More... #include <ernie/scene/brdf.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::string description std::function< std::uint32_t(std::span< const float >)> features The layers a material of these parameters uses, as bits, for models whose layers cost nothing where no material has them: the renderer compiles the model with BRDF_FEATURES defined as the union over the scene's materials of it (so code under a bit none has falls away), and gives each material's own to BrdfParams::features . std::string id Stable identifier used in settings, e.g. "hapke". std::string name Display name. std::vector< BrdfParam > params std::vector< std::string > references std::string slang std::function< glm::vec3(std::span< const float >)> subsurfaceRadius For models that scatter light beneath their surfaces ( BrdfRegistry::kSubsurfaceFeature ): how far, per linear RGB channel in scene units, for a material of these parameters; the renderer spreads its subsurface light over this radius, per band. std::string typeName Slang struct implementing IBrdf , e.g. Public Functions Type Name std::vector< std::size_t > Colours () const The indices of its colour parameters' red ones, in order. std::vector< float > Defaults () const Default value of every parameter, in order. Detailed Description slang is a Slang module that may import brdf; ( BrdfSlang ) and defines a struct named typeName implementing IBrdf , whose radianceFactor(BrdfInput s, BrdfParams p) returns the radiance factor I/F (pi times the bidirectional reflectance) for unit incident irradiance. Parameter i , in the order of params , is p.get(i) . BrdfInput carries cos(i), cos(e), cos(g), the cosine of the azimuth between the incidence and emission planes, an rgb albedo input whose meaning each model documents, and the variance per axis of surface slopes finer than the renderer resolves (a filtered normal map's), which models with a roughness add to it ( widenedMeanSlope for Hapke-like ones) and others may ignore. A model only defines radianceFactor ; every render backend evaluates and samples it through the generic helpers of the brdf module ( evaluateBrdf , sampleBrdf , brdfPdf ), so a model works unchanged in the rasterizer and in ray and path tracers. CameraView RasterView (double overscan=1.0) const The raster view: the inverse pose, and a projection with the focal length divided by overscan (so with lens distortion it covers the undistorted rays of every sensor pixel), the principal point and the clipping range. CameraView RasterView (const glm::dmat4 & pose, double overscan) const RasterView from camera-to-world pose in place of transform , such as one view of a batch, without copying the camera. void SetVerticalFov (double radians) Sets the vertical aperture so the image spans radians vertically at the focal length. double SubframeTime (int subframe) const The time of sub-frame subframe in frames relative to the frame's: evenly spaced from the top row's opening to the bottom row's closing, the last at shutterClose . int Subframes () const The sub-frames a frame renders: 1 with the shutter closed (open equal to close) and a global shutter, else shutterSamples , at least 2. double VerticalFov () const The vertical field of view in radians. Detailed Description The pose transform maps camera to world coordinates; as in USD the camera looks down its -z axis with +y up. Interactive controls such as OrbitController write it. Focal length and apertures are read in millimetres. The image fits the vertical aperture: pixels are square with a pitch of verticalAperture / height , and the horizontal aperture follows from the image's aspect. Aperture offsets shift the principal point. An orthographic camera follows UsdGeomCamera (and GfCamera): its apertures and their offsets are in tenths of a scene unit, the size of the view in the scene, and it has no focal length; every ray runs along the view direction. Its optics are telecentric, without fall-off off axis or depth of field, and its pixels have the pitch orthographicPixelPitchUm on the sensor. Its lens has no distortion. Distances to the camera are from its image plane. Terrain levels of detail still follow the distance from the camera's position, so place it near what it sees. Radiometry follows the camera equation: a scene radiance L reaches the sensor as irradiance E = L pi t cos^4(theta) / (4 N^2) for an object far away, with transmission t, f-number N and field angle theta; a pixel collects E times its area times the exposure time, converted to photons and electrons per band. The photographic outputs instead scale luminance by USD's linear exposure scale; with a one-channel (monochrome) sensor they are grey, weighting the bands by that channel's quantum efficiency, scaled so a flat spectrum keeps its luminance. docs.text: The pose transform maps camera to world coordinates; as in USD the camera looks down its -z axis with +y up. Interactive controls such as OrbitController write it. Focal length and apertures are read in millimetres. The image fits the vertical aperture: pixels are square with a pitch of verticalAperture / height , and the horizontal aperture follows from the image's aspect. Aperture offsets shift the principal point. An orthographic camera follows UsdGeomCamera (and GfCamera): its apertures and their offsets are in tenths of a scene unit, the size of the view in the scene, and it has no focal length; every ray runs along the view direction. Its optics are telecentric, without fall-off off axis or depth of field, and its pixels have the pitch orthographicPixelPitchUm on the sensor. Its lens has no distortion. Distances to the camera are from its image plane. Terrain levels of detail still follow the distance from the camera's position, so place it near what it sees. Radiometry follows the camera equation: a scene radiance L reaches the sensor as irradiance E = L pi t cos^4(theta) / (4 N^2) for an object far away, with transmission t, f-number N and field angle theta; a pixel collects E times its area times the exposure time, converted to photons and electrons per band. The photographic outputs instead scale luminance by USD's linear exposure scale; with a one-channel (monochrome) sensor they are grey, weighting the bands by that channel's quantum efficiency, scaled so a flat spectrum keeps its luminance. References: * B. K. P. Horn, "Robot Vision", MIT Press, 1986 (the image irradiance equation E = L (pi / 4) (d / f)^2 cos^4(alpha), with N = f / d). * Pixar, "UsdGeomCamera", https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_camera.html

Public Static Functions Type Name glm::dvec3 FaceDirection (std::uint32_t face, double s, double t) Unit direction of the point ( s , t ) of face face , both in [-1, 1]. std::pair< std::uint32_t, glm::dvec2 > FacePoint (const glm::dvec3 & direction) The face holding direction , which need not be unit length, and its (s, t) there. Detailed Description Coordinates are the body-fixed frame: z towards the north pole and x towards longitude 0, in the same units as the radius. Each face is a grid of FaceCells() x FaceCells() quads whose FaceCells() + 1 squared vertices carry heights above the radius; vertex ( col , row ) of face f lies in direction FaceDirection(f, s, t) with s = 2 col / FaceCells() - 1 and t = 2 row / FaceCells() - 1. Vertices on an edge or corner of the cube appear on every face sharing it and must carry the same height there. Faces 0 to 3 straddle the equator, centred on longitudes 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees east, with columns running east and rows running south. Face 4 is centred on the north pole and face 5 on the south pole. On every face, column x row points into the body, so all faces wind the same way. Adjacent faces may run their grids in opposite directions along a shared edge. The projection is equiangular (Ronchi et al. 1996): s and t map to the face plane through tan(pi s / 4), so cells span nearly equal angles and areas differ by at most a factor of about 1.4 over a face, against 5.2 for a plain gnomonic cube. Grid lines are great circles. Select runs Strugar's algorithm on all six trees, using distances to each node's CubeSphereRegion . Neighbouring patches, across faces too, differ by at most one level when the first range is at least MinFirstRange . Odd vertices of a patch morph in 3D towards the midpoint of their two neighbours on the next coarser level: along the patch's edges these are the edge's own neighbours, and for vertices odd in both directions those on the quad diagonal from (1, 0) to (0, 1). Unlike the flat terrain's slide towards lower indices, this does not depend on which way a face's grid runs, so edges between faces match, and a fully morphed patch is exactly the coarser mesh. Refinement ( SetRefinement ) adds levels finer than the data: with k extra levels each face is a grid of FineCells() = 2^k FaceCells() quads, the data's vertices every 2^k of its lines and heights between them interpolated, so the surface keeps its shape (the sphere's curvature and the data's heights) down to cells 2^k times smaller than the data's near the eye. Levels then count from the finest, a data level l being level l + k, and patches' origins are on the fine grid. A refined node's heights are its data leaf's. The body may be an ellipsoid ( SetRadii ), triaxial or not: the cube's grid stays the same in direction, a height of 0 lies on the ellipsoid along the vertex's direction ( BasePoint ), and heights rise along the ellipsoid's geodetic normal there ( SurfaceNormal ). Node regions widen by bounds on how much the surface radius and the normal's tilt can vary, so selection stays conservative. Positions on a planet need more precision than single floats. Selection works in doubles, and its frustum is relative to the eye: build it from a view-projection matrix whose view has the eye at the origin and the body frame's axes. References: * C. Ronchi, R. Iacono and P. S. Paolucci, "The 'Cubed Sphere': A New Method for the Solution of Partial Differential Equations in Spherical Geometry", Journal of Computational Physics 124(1):93-114, 1996. https://doi.org/10.1006/jcph.1996.0047 * P. Cozzi and K. Ring, "3D Engine Design for Virtual Globes", A K Peters/CRC Press, 2011, chapter 2 (the ellipsoid's geodetic normal, proportional to x_i / a_i^2). https://doi.org/10.1201/9781439865583 * M. Lambers and A. Kolb, "Ellipsoidal Cube Maps for Accurate Rendering of Planetary-Scale Terrain Data", Pacific Graphics 2012 Short Papers, 5-10 (a cube-map quadtree on an ellipsoid). https://diglib.eg.org/handle/10.2312/PE.PG.PG2012short.005-010 * F. docs.text: Coordinates are the body-fixed frame: z towards the north pole and x towards longitude 0, in the same units as the radius. Each face is a grid of FaceCells() x FaceCells() quads whose FaceCells() + 1 squared vertices carry heights above the radius; vertex ( col , row ) of face f lies in direction FaceDirection(f, s, t) with s = 2 col / FaceCells() - 1 and t = 2 row / FaceCells() - 1. Vertices on an edge or corner of the cube appear on every face sharing it and must carry the same height there. Faces 0 to 3 straddle the equator, centred on longitudes 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees east, with columns running east and rows running south. Face 4 is centred on the north pole and face 5 on the south pole. On every face, column x row points into the body, so all faces wind the same way. Adjacent faces may run their grids in opposite directions along a shared edge. The projection is equiangular (Ronchi et al. 1996): s and t map to the face plane through tan(pi s / 4), so cells span nearly equal angles and areas differ by at most a factor of about 1.4 over a face, against 5.2 for a plain gnomonic cube. Grid lines are great circles. Select runs Strugar's algorithm on all six trees, using distances to each node's CubeSphereRegion . Neighbouring patches, across faces too, differ by at most one level when the first range is at least MinFirstRange . Odd vertices of a patch morph in 3D towards the midpoint of their two neighbours on the next coarser level: along the patch's edges these are the edge's own neighbours, and for vertices odd in both directions those on the quad diagonal from (1, 0) to (0, 1). Unlike the flat terrain's slide towards lower indices, this does not depend on which way a face's grid runs, so edges between faces match, and a fully morphed patch is exactly the coarser mesh. Refinement ( SetRefinement ) adds levels finer than the data: with k extra levels each face is a grid of FineCells() = 2^k FaceCells() quads, the data's vertices every 2^k of its lines and heights between them interpolated, so the surface keeps its shape (the sphere's curvature and the data's heights) down to cells 2^k times smaller than the data's near the eye. Levels then count from the finest, a data level l being level l + k, and patches' origins are on the fine grid. A refined node's heights are its data leaf's. The body may be an ellipsoid ( SetRadii ), triaxial or not: the cube's grid stays the same in direction, a height of 0 lies on the ellipsoid along the vertex's direction ( BasePoint ), and heights rise along the ellipsoid's geodetic normal there ( SurfaceNormal ). Node regions widen by bounds on how much the surface radius and the normal's tilt can vary, so selection stays conservative. Positions on a planet need more precision than single floats. Selection works in doubles, and its frustum is relative to the eye: build it from a view-projection matrix whose view has the eye at the origin and the body frame's axes. References: * C. Ronchi, R. Iacono and P. S. Paolucci, "The 'Cubed Sphere': A New Method for the Solution of Partial Differential Equations in Spherical Geometry", Journal of Computational Physics 124(1):93-114, 1996. https://doi.org/10.1006/jcph.1996.0047 * P. Cozzi and K. Ring, "3D Engine Design for Virtual Globes", A K Peters/CRC Press, 2011, chapter 2 (the ellipsoid's geodetic normal, proportional to x_i / a_i^2). https://doi.org/10.1201/9781439865583 * M. Lambers and A. Kolb, "Ellipsoidal Cube Maps for Accurate Rendering of Planetary-Scale Terrain Data", Pacific Graphics 2012 Short Papers, 5-10 (a cube-map quadtree on an ellipsoid). https://diglib.eg.org/handle/10.2312/PE.PG.PG2012short.005-010 * F. CUDA work runs in the device's primary context, the one CUDA frameworks use, on the legacy default stream, so it is ordered after work that frameworks hand over through DLPack. Signals to Vulkan all go on the legacy stream, after an event recorded on the stream the work ran on, so values arrive in order however many streams write. docs.text: The CUDA driver (libcuda) is loaded at run time, so Ernie has no build dependency on the CUDA toolkit; without an NVIDIA driver Create reports CUDA unavailable. CUDA work runs in the device's primary context, the one CUDA frameworks use, on the legacy default stream, so it is ordered after work that frameworks hand over through DLPack. Signals to Vulkan all go on the legacy stream, after an event recorded on the stream the work ran on, so values arrive in order however many streams write. Reference: NVIDIA, CUDA Driver API, "External Resource Interoperability", https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__EXTRES__INTEROP.html

docs.text: Struct ernie::DropletPhaseTable ClassList > ernie > DropletPhaseTable The phase function of a cloud's water droplets in each of a frame's bands, for volumes to read (volume.slang's dropletAt ): Mie scattering by a gamma distribution of droplet radii, its narrow forward peak (within kDropletForwardDegrees ) folded into the extinction as unscattered light. More... #include <ernie/util/cloud_phase.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::size_t angles = 0 Samples of each row, at scattering angles theta(u) = pi / 2 (1 - cos pi u), u = i / (angles - 1): dense about the forward and backward directions, where the peaks are. double forwardFraction = 0.0 The share of the light the forward peak scattered, the bands' mean, which the extinction loses (times 1 - it). std::vector< float > values Rows of angles values (sr^-1): each band's, its peak kept, over 1 - its share (integrating to 1 / (1 - it)); then the bands' mean, its peak folded away (integrating to 1), for light scattered many times, whose colours blur. Detailed Description The silver lining, the bright sheen opposite the sun on cloud tops, the fogbow near 140 degrees and the glory at 180 come from its lobes. Each band's row, for single scattering, keeps the peak (as Bouthors et al. add it back for light scattered once), over the extinction less its share; the bands' mean, for light scattered many times, has it folded away. References: * A. Bouthors, F. Neyret and S. Lefebvre, "Real-time realistic illumination and shading of stratiform clouds", Eurographics Workshop on Natural Phenomena 2006 (the droplets' gamma distribution, and the forward peak folded into the extinction, their "modified Mie"). * A. Bouthors, F. Neyret, N. Max, E. Bruneton and C. Crassin, "Interactive multiple anisotropic scattering in clouds", ACM SIGGRAPH Symposium on Interactive 3D Graphics and Games 2008. * J. E. Hansen and L. D. Travis, "Light scattering in planetary atmospheres", Space Science Reviews 16(4):527-610, 1974, section 2.4 (distributions alike in effective radius and variance scatter alike: the gamma's as a log-normal's). https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00168069 Public Attributes Documentation variable angles Samples of each row, at scattering angles theta(u) = pi / 2 (1 - cos pi u), u = i / (angles - 1): dense about the forward and backward directions, where the peaks are. std::size_t ernie::DropletPhaseTable::angles; variable forwardFraction The share of the light the forward peak scattered, the bands' mean, which the extinction loses (times 1 - it). double ernie::DropletPhaseTable::forwardFraction; variable values Rows of angles values (sr^-1): each band's, its peak kept, over 1 - its share (integrating to 1 / (1 - it)); then the bands' mean, its peak folded away (integrating to 1), for light scattered many times, whose colours blur. std::vector<float> ernie::DropletPhaseTable::values; The documentation for this class was generated from the following file ernie/util/cloud_phase.h

docs.text: Class ernie::EditHistory ClassList > ernie > EditHistory Undo and redo for scene edits made through it: attribute sets and clears, prims defined, and prims removed with their descendants. More... #include <ernie/scene/edit_history.h> Public Functions Type Name void Add ( Scene & scene, const Scene & source, const Path & path) Copies the prim at path of source and its descendants, with their attributes and tensors (shared), to the same path of scene and records it; undoing removes them. void BeginGroup () Groups the edits until EndGroup into one step. bool CanRedo () const bool CanUndo () const void Clear ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute) Clears attribute of the prim at path (back to its fallback) and records it. void Close () Ends the open step, so the next edit starts a new one. void Define ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view type) Defines the prim at path with type and records it; undoing removes it. void EndGroup () bool Redo ( Scene & scene) Redoes the last undone step (or group); returns whether there was one. std::string RedoLabel () const bool Remove ( Scene & scene, const Path & path) Removes the prim at path and its descendants and records them; undoing restores them, sharing their tensors. void Reset () Forgets every step, such as when the viewer switches scenes. void Set ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, Value value, bool open=false) Sets attribute of the prim at path to value and records it, dropping what was undone (the redo steps). void Set ( Scene & scene, const Path & path, std::vector< std::pair< std::string, Value > > edits, bool open=false) Sets several attributes of the prim at path , such as the transform ops of LocalTransformEdits , as one step. std::size_t Size () const The number of steps recorded, counting a group's edits one by one. bool Undo ( Scene & scene) Undoes the last step (or group); returns whether there was one. std::string UndoLabel () const A short description of the step Undo would undo, such as "/World/Cube xformOp:transform". Detailed Description Each records what it changes, so Undo puts it back (an attribute's earlier value, or none; a removed subtree with its attributes and tensors) and Redo does it again. Continuous edits, such as dragging a slider or a gizmo, merge into one step: an open edit of the same attribute as the last step updates that step until Close (called when the drag ends). Edits between BeginGroup and EndGroup , such as defining a prim and setting its attributes, undo and redo together. Edits made to the scene directly are not recorded; undoing past one sets the attribute to what the history last saw. Reference: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson and J. Vlissides, "Design Patterns", the Command pattern, Addison-Wesley, 1994.
