docs.text: Class ernie::FrameUploads ClassList > ernie > FrameUploads Host data bound for device buffers, staged for one frame in flight and copied by that frame's own commands ( Record ), so the host can prepare a frame while the device still runs earlier ones that read the same buffers: the copies wait on the device for that earlier work, in queue order, rather than the host waiting for it. More... #include <ernie/device/frame_uploads.h> Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr std::uint32_t kSlots = 2 Frames that may be in flight at once. Public Functions Type Name void Begin (std::uint32_t slot) Starts staging into slot slot (below kSlots ), whose previous frame must have finished on the device. FrameUploads (const VulkanContext & context) VkDeviceSize Pending () const Bytes staged since the last Record . void Record (VkCommandBuffer commands) Records the staged copies, in order, between barriers: before, against every earlier command's access (including earlier submissions'), and after, making the copies visible to every later command. std::uint32_t Slot () const The slot of the last Begin . void Write (const GpuBuffer & destination, std::span< const std::byte > bytes, VkDeviceSize offset=0) Stages bytes for destination at offset ; the copy is recorded by the next Record , and dropped if destination is destroyed or replaced first. Detailed Description Writes keep their order, so a buffer written in part, or twice, ends as if written in place. Each of kSlots slots has its own staging memory. A frame takes a slot with Begin once the frame that last used that slot has finished; writes until its Record stage there. References: * Khronos, "Synchronization Examples", transfer then use in a later submission. https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/wiki/Synchronization-Examples * A. More... #include <ernie/util/noise.h> Public Functions Type Name double Fbm (const glm::dvec3 & p, int octaves=5, double lacunarity=2.0, double gain=0.5) const Fractional Brownian motion: octaves layers of the noise, each lacunarity times the frequency and gain times the amplitude of the one before, the first at p itself; divided by the sum of the amplitudes, so within about [-1, 1] too. GradientNoise (std::uint32_t seed=0) The noise of seed : its permutation of the lattice. const std::array< std::uint8_t, 512 > & Permutation () const Its lattice's permutation, 256 entries twice over, for shaders to evaluate the same noise on the GPU. double operator() (const glm::dvec3 & p) const The noise at p . Detailed Description The same seed gives the same noise everywhere, from C++ or Python ( ernie.fbm_noise ), so demo twins build the same fields. References: * K. IsdCameraModel ( IsdSensor isd) glm::dvec3 LookAt (double time, double line, double sample) const The unit body-fixed direction of the ray at time through detector line line and sample sample ( IsdLineScanner::Look ). glm::dvec2 PixelOf (glm::dvec2 focal) const Image (line on the detector, sample) of distorted focal plane point focal . glm::dmat4 PoseAt (double time, const glm::dmat3 & axes) const The camera-to-body pose of Ernie's camera on axes at time . Protected Static Functions Type Name glm::dquat RotationAt (const IsdRotation & rotation, double time) The rotation rotation describes at time : its constant after its time-dependent part. Detailed Description Image coordinates are CSM's: (line, sample) with the first pixel's centre at (0.5, 0.5). The sensor's position is sampled as usgscsm samples it: at least 25 even times over the states, each a cubic Hermite of the states around it (ALE's spline) rotated into the body's frame, then interpolated eighth-order Lagrange (fewer points near the ends). Its orientation, sensor to body = body rotation x inverse pointing, is taken at the union of their times (each interpolated along the great arc), resampled evenly and interpolated the same way. Detector line d and sample s lie on the focal plane at the inverse of focal2pixel of (d x line summing + starting detector line - detector centre line, s x sample summing + starting detector sample - detector centre sample), in mm; the lens's distortion moves it; the camera looks along (-x, -y, -f) in the sensor's frame. Light-time and aberration corrections are left out, as usgscsm leaves them out. Detailed Description Unlike the line scanner, the camera looks along (x, y, f) in the sensor's frame, and a ray meets the ellipsoid at its first intersection along it. A rolling shutter's jitter ( jitter ), as usgscsm models it, moves each image line's pixels by an offset polynomial in the line's exposure time, the pose left at the centre time: image coordinates less the jitter are the unjittered camera's. References: * usgscsm's UsgsAstroFrameSensorModel ( imageToGround , groundToImage , losEllipsoidIntersect , constructStateFromIsd ), and its src/Utilities.cpp ( removeJitter , addJitter ). Public Functions Documentation function GroundToImage The image coordinates (line, sample) of body-fixed point ground , the jitter added by fixed-point iteration as usgscsm's addJitter (to 1e-10 pixels). glm::dvec2 ernie::IsdFrame::GroundToImage ( const glm::dvec3 & ground ) const function ImageTime Ephemeris seconds at which the image is exposed: the ISD's centre time. inline double ernie::IsdFrame::ImageTime () const function ImageToGround Where pixel ( line , sample )'s ray first meets the body's ellipsoid raised by height metres, or the ray's point nearest the ellipsoid when it misses. glm::dvec3 ernie::IsdFrame::ImageToGround ( double line, double sample, double height=0.0 ) const function IsdFrame explicit ernie::IsdFrame::IsdFrame ( IsdSensor isd ) Exception: std::invalid_argument if isd is not a frame camera's, or as IsdCameraModel . function Jitter The rolling shutter's jitter (line, sample) at image line line , pixels, as usgscsm's removeJitter takes it: the polynomials at the exposure time of line round( line ) (clamped to the ISD's lines); zero without jitter. glm::dvec2 ernie::IsdFrame::Jitter ( double line ) const function Look The unit body-fixed direction of pixel ( line , sample )'s ray, its jitter removed. glm::dvec3 ernie::IsdFrame::Look ( double line, double sample ) const function View The image as Ernie renders it: a frame camera of the image's samples by its lines, its exposure left as authored (frame ISDs carry none). FrameView ernie::IsdFrame::View () const The jitter is a shift of each line's pixels, which Ernie's camera cannot take exactly: a rolling shutter ( rollingShutter ) moves the pose linearly across the rows, while usgscsm keeps the pose and moves the pixels by a polynomial in time. So its midrange over the lines moves the principal point and the rest, half its range, is added to distortionResidualPixels . docs.text: Struct ernie::IsdLineScanner::Strip ClassList > ernie > IsdLineScanner > Strip A strip of lines image lines from firstLine as Ernie renders it: a pushbroom camera ( CameraParams::pushbroom ) whose rows are those lines, posed from at the strip's first line's start and to at its end (camera to body-fixed world). More... #include <ernie/scene/isd.h> Public Attributes Type Name CameraParams camera double distortionResidualPixels = 0.0 The fitted distortion's largest departure from the ISD's along the line, in pixels. glm::dmat4 from = {1.0} double fromTime = 0.0 glm::dmat4 to = {1.0} double toTime = 0.0 Detailed Description Consecutive strips chain: each's from is the last one's to , so stepping the camera's transform through the strips' to s (after a first step at the first from ) renders the image strip by strip. The pose between from and to is a straight line and a great-arc turn, which departs from the orbit's curve by about a T^2 / 8 for its acceleration a over the strip's time T: keep strips short (for LRO's NAC, 64 lines are 0.8 s and 0.1 m). The lens's distortion along the detector and off it is fitted as the camera's Brown-Conrady k1 to k3, p1 and p2, which the pushbroom's lens resamples through (rows of points off the line from the time that sees them). docs.text: In the rasterizer, distant lights get cascades over a single view, or orthographic maps over the scene in a batch; sphere lights a perspective map when their cone is at most kMaxSpotConeDegrees , else six (a cube); rect and disk lights a cube at their centre. The rasterizer shades rect and disk lights with their exact Lambertian irradiance, the vector form factor of the emitter clipped to the receiver's horizon (Lambert's polygon formula; Arvo 1994), and the receiver's BRDF evaluated along that vector. Disks are integrated as 16-gons of the same area. Reference: J. Arvo, "The Irradiance Jacobian for Partially Occluded Polyhedral Sources", SIGGRAPH '94, 343-350, 1994. https://doi.org/10.1145/192161.192250

docs.text: Struct ernie::LightPatternModel ClassList > ernie > LightPatternModel A laser's pattern written in Slang: the relative power a laser sends towards each direction, its watts, beam and shadows staying Ernie's. More... #include <ernie/scene/light_pattern.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::string description double extent = 1.0 The largest |x / z| and |y / z| it lights: it emits nothing beyond, and its shadow view covers that much. std::string id The ernie:laser:pattern naming it. std::string name bool normalized = false Its emission integrates to 1 over the whole tangent plane, whatever its parameters and footprint, so Ernie need not integrate it (the built-in spot, line and grid). std::vector< LightPatternParam > params std::string slang Its module's source. std::string typeName The Slang struct implementing it. Public Functions Type Name std::vector< float > Defaults () const Default value of every parameter, in order. Detailed Description slang is a Slang module that may import light_pattern; ( LightPatternSlang ) and defines a struct named typeName implementing ILightPattern , whose gives the relative power per unit area of the tangent plane (x / z, y / z along the laser's x and y, z along its beam) at input.t , averaged over a pixel's footprint input.footprint wide in it (so features finer than a pixel keep their power), at the laser's input.wavelength (nm) and the frame's input.time on the sensor clock (s). input.beam is the beam's own 1/e^2 radius there, w(z) / z, which a pattern of beamlets draws each one with ( beamlet ); a continuous pattern can ignore it. A laser with a sequence ( ernie:laser:sequence:count ) shows its frame input.frame of input.frames (0 of 1 without one), the frames its exposure spans weighted by their time in it. Its scale does not matter: Ernie integrates it over |t| < extent on the GPU, averaged over its sequence's frames, so the laser emits its power's ernie:laser:efficiency into it (its ernie:laser:zeroOrder going into an undiffracted spot), unless normalized says it integrates to 1 already. Parameter i is p.get(i) ; the laser's ernie:laser:pattern:data is p.data(i) ( p.dataCount() of them) and its ernie:laser:pattern:image p.image(uv, footprint) . Detailed Description A level-0 node spans leafCells x leafCells grid quads; a level-L node spans leafCells * 2^L and the single root node covers the whole raster. The tree stores only each node's min and max height, so selection can bound nodes in 3D for range and frustum tests. Select walks the tree from the root and picks, for each region, the coarsest level whose range covers it (Strugar 2009, algorithm 1). Every node is drawn as its four quarters, so all patches share one PatchCells() grid and differ only in origin and vertex spacing. Within each level's range the vertex shader morphs vertices towards the next coarser level, so switching level never pops; see terrain.slang . With a first range of at least MinFirstRange , neighbouring patches differ by at most one level and their shared edges match exactly, so no skirts or stitching are needed. References: * F. Strugar, "Continuous Distance-Dependent Level of Detail for Rendering Heightmaps", Journal of Graphics, GPU, and Game Tools 14(4):57-74, 2009. https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2009.10129287 * P. Lindstrom, D. Koller, W. Ribarsky, L. F. Hodges, N. Faust and G. A. docs.text: Struct ernie::MaterialXShader ClassList > ernie > MaterialXShader A MaterialX surface's shading as Slang for Ernie's shading pass: void ernieMaterialX(out float3 color, out float3 transparency) , which evaluates its graph for the pixel being shaded through the functions below (which the shading pass defines before it), with MaterialX's own closures and nodes: More... #include <ernie/session/materialx.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::string code std::vector< std::string > geomProps Primvar names, by id. bool surface = false Whether it is a surface (lit by its closures) rather than a pattern or value shown as it is. std::vector< MaterialXTexture > textures bool transparent = false Whether it may be transparent (MaterialX's isTransparentSurface). std::uint32_t uniformBytes = 0 std::vector< MaterialXUniform > uniforms Detailed Description ernieMxPositionWorld(), ernieMxNormalWorld(), ernieMxTangentWorld(), ernieMxBitangentWorld() and their *Object() versions (float3); ernieMxTexcoord(int set) (float2); ernieMxColor(int set) (float4); ernieMxGeomPropFloat(int id), ...Float2, ...Float3, ...Float4 and ...Int, the primvars geomProps names by id; ernieMxViewPosition() (float3), ernieMxTime() and ernieMxFrame() (float). ernieMxLoadFloat(uint offset), ...Int, ...Float2, ...Float3, ...Float4, ...Float3x3 and ...Float4x4: the uniform buffer's values. ernieMxSample(uint slot, float2 uv), ernieMxSampleLevel(uint slot, float2 uv, float lod), ernieMxSampleGrad(uint slot, float2 uv, float2 dx, float2 dy) (float4) and ernieMxTextureSize(uint slot, int level) (int2): the texture table's. ernieMxLightCount() (int); ernieMxLightDirection(int light) (float3, towards it; zero for one that cannot light the pixel); ernieMxLightResponse(int light, float3 response): the surface's response to a unit of the light's radiant intensity, which the shading pass scales by the light's spectrum, distance and shadow. ernieMxEnvironmentRadiance(float3 direction, float alpha) and ernieMxEnvironmentIrradiance(float3 normal) (float3): the light from all around (dome, sky and ambient light), as a GGX lobe of roughness alpha about direction and as cosine-weighted irradiance over pi. color is what leaves the surface towards the eye, but for the lights' share (reported per light): its emission and environment light. Colours are linear Rec. 709, as MaterialX's are. docs.text: Struct ernie::MeshDataOptions ClassList > ernie > MeshDataOptions The geometry of the Mesh prim at mesh : points , faceVertexCounts and faceVertexIndices (triangulated as fans), per-vertex normals , and per-vertex primvars:displayColor when it has one colour per point. More... #include <ernie/session/resolve.h> Public Attributes Type Name bool posed = true Pose a skinned mesh (on the CPU); false keeps its rest points, for the GPU to pose. RefinementStencils * stencils = nullptr Where a subdivision surface's refinement stencils go, if anywhere ( Subdivide ); left empty for other meshes. Detailed Description Points , normals and colours may be float32 or float64, shaped (n, 3) or flat; indices int32, int64 or uint32. Normals and colours of other sizes (such as face-varying ones) are ignored. Points on a CUDA device come back as zeros of the right number, for the caller to copy device to device. Texture coordinates come per triangle corner from primvars:<set> (constant, uniform, vertex or faceVarying, optionally indexed; see tokens.h ), the set being the one the bound material's textures read, else st . Exception: std::invalid_argument naming the attribute for arrays of the wrong type, size or device, or invalid topology. For a UsdGeom primitive ( Cube , Sphere , Cylinder , Cone , Capsule , Plane ) the generated mesh, PrimitiveMeshOf . A Mesh with a subdivisionScheme is its limit surface instead, refined by OpenSubdiv at SubdivisionLevelOf ( Subdivide ), its normals the surface's. A skinned Mesh ( skel:skeleton ) is posed at the stage's time code, before it is refined, unless options say otherwise. docs.text: Struct ernie::NanoVdbGrid ClassList > ernie > NanoVdbGrid One sparse grid as NanoVDB lays it out: a buffer the GPU reads in place (PNanoVDB's tree walk), and what Ernie needs of its header. More... #include <ernie/util/nanovdb.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::vector< std::uint8_t > buffer The grid itself, from its GridData header on, padded to a multiple of 8 bytes; empty when only its head was read ( NanoVdbGridHead ). bool hasStatistics = false Whether the grid carries its values' statistics (NanoVDB's HAS_MIN_MAX flag; Warp's grids do not). glm::ivec3 indexMax = {-1} glm::ivec3 indexMin = {0} The active values' bounds in index space, inclusive; empty (min > max) for a grid without active values. glm::dmat4 indexToGrid = {1.0} Index coordinates to the grid's frame, from the grid's map (doubles). double maxValue = 0.0 double minValue = 0.0 With them, the smallest and largest active value of a scalar grid (the root's; for vector grids, of their lengths); else 0. std::string name std::uint64_t size = 0 The grid's bytes, as its header gives them. NanoVdbType type = NanoVdbType::Unknown glm::dvec3 voxelSize = {1.0} The size of a voxel in the grid's frame. Public Functions Type Name bool Empty () const Whether the grid holds active values. void GridBounds (glm::dvec3 & min, glm::dvec3 & max) const The active bounds in the grid's frame: the index bounds grown by a voxel on every side (what trilinear sampling reaches), through indexToGrid . bool Scalar () const Whether volumes sample it as one value per voxel. bool Vector () const Whether volumes sample it as a 3-vector per voxel. Detailed Description Index space puts a value at each integer coordinate; the grid's map takes index coordinates to the grid's own frame (OpenVDB's "world", which a Volume prim's transform then places). Museth, "VDB: High-Resolution Sparse Volumes with Dynamic Topology", ACM Transactions on Graphics 32(3), 27, 2013. https://doi.org/10.1145/2487228.2487235 * NanoVDB's file layout, nanovdb/io/IO.h and FileMetaData in nanovdb/NanoVDB.h, OpenVDB 13.0.0. More... #include <ernie/scene/orbit_controller.h> Public Attributes Type Name double distance = /* multi line expression */ World units from the eye to the target. float pitch = /* multi line expression */ Radians, clamped to [kMinPitch, kMaxPitch]. glm::dvec3 target = {0.0} float verticalFov = 0.785398f Radians. float yaw = 0.0f Radians. Public Static Attributes Type Name constexpr double kMaxDistance = 1e21 constexpr float kMaxPitch = 1.55f constexpr double kMinDistance = 1e-3 The orbit distance's range: a millimetre to about 100,000 light-years. constexpr float kMinPitch = -1.55f Pitch stops short of straight down and up, where the view's up vector degenerates; views may look up from below the ground. Public Functions Type Name void Apply ( CameraParams & camera) const Sets camera 's transform, vertical field of view (through its aperture, keeping its focal length) and clipping range. glm::dvec3 Eye () const Eye position in world coordinates. double FarPlane () const void Frame (const glm::dvec3 & boundsMin, const glm::dvec3 & boundsMax) Aims at the centre of the axis-aligned box [ boundsMin , boundsMax ] from a distance at which its bounding sphere fits the vertical field of view with a small margin. void FrameView (const glm::dvec3 & boundsMin, const glm::dvec3 & boundsMax, double aspect) Aims at the centre of the box [ boundsMin , boundsMax ] from the current direction, at the distance where all its corners fit a view aspect (width over height) wide with a small margin: a flat or long box fills the view rather than its bounding sphere. CameraParams MakeCamera (std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) const A default camera of width x height with this pose, field of view and clipping range. double NearPlane () const Clipping planes scaled to the orbit distance. void Orbit (float deltaYaw, float deltaPitch) Rotates by deltaYaw and deltaPitch radians, clamping pitch. void Pan (float dx, float dy, float viewportHeight) Moves the target parallel to the ground by a screen-space drag of ( dx , dy ) pixels in a viewport viewportHeight pixels tall, so the terrain follows the cursor at the target depth. void PanVertical (float dx, float dy, float viewportHeight) Moves the target across the screen by a drag of ( dx , dy ) pixels: sideways as Pan , and up and down along world z. glm::dmat4 Transform () const Camera-to-world transform of the eye looking at the target, +z up. void Zoom (float steps) Zooms by steps scroll steps; positive moves closer. Detailed Description It holds no camera of its own: Apply writes its pose, field of view and clipping range into one. Yaw rotates around the vertical axis (0 looks north, positive turns the view clockwise seen from above); pitch is the elevation angle of the eye above the target's horizontal plane. The target and distance are double precision, as the scene's transforms are, so the view orbits as smoothly light-years from the origin as at it (the renderer draws relative to a floating origin near the eye). docs.text: Class ernie::PagePool ClassList > ernie > PagePool The software path of virtual textures, for devices without sparse residency and textures larger than the device's images: resident tiles live in pages, the layers of one 2D array image, which shaders find through a page table ( VirtualTexture ) and filter themselves (bilinear within a page, trilinear across two mips). PagePool & operator= (const PagePool &) = delete ~PagePool () override Public Functions inherited from ernie::TileStore See ernie::TileStore Type Name virtual bool Bound (const SparseTile & tile) const = 0 virtual std::size_t BoundTiles () const = 0 virtual VkDeviceSize Bytes () const = 0 Device memory held. virtual void Release (std::span< const SparseTile > tiles) = 0 Frees tiles now; no work in flight may read them. virtual std::uint32_t TailMip () const = 0 The first mip in the tail. virtual std::uint32_t TileBorder () const = 0 Texels of the neighbouring tiles written around each tile ( TileDataBytes counts them), so filtering stays inside it. virtual VkExtent2D TileCount (std::uint32_t mip) const = 0 Tiles across and down mip mip (below TailMip ). virtual VkDeviceSize TileDataBytes (const SparseTile & tile) const = 0 Bytes of the texels (or blocks) Write takes for tile . virtual VkExtent2D TileExtent (const SparseTile & tile) const = 0 Texels across and down tile , a whole tile but where it overhangs its mip's right or bottom edge. virtual VkDeviceSize TileMemoryBytes () const = 0 Device memory a tile takes. virtual VkExtent2D TileTexels () const = 0 Texels along a tile's sides. virtual void Write (std::span< const SparseTile > tiles, std::span< const std::span< const std::byte > > texels) = 0 Makes tiles resident, writing texels[i] into tile i , for work submitted after it to read. virtual void WriteTail (std::span< const std::span< const std::byte > > mips) = 0 Writes the tail: mips[i] holds mip TailMip() + i . virtual ~TileStore () = default Detailed Description A page is kPageTexels square: a kTileTexels tile with a border of kBorder texels from its neighbours (clamped at the texture's edges), so bilinear filtering near a tile's edge stays in its page. Writes are copied in submissions the host does not wait for, ordered before work submitted after them. Reference: J. M. P. van Waveren, "Software Virtual Textures", id Software, 2012. docs.text: A page is kPageTexels square: a kTileTexels tile with a border of kBorder texels from its neighbours (clamped at the texture's edges), so bilinear filtering near a tile's edge stays in its page. Every size is a whole number of 4 x 4 blocks, so BC tiles are cut from BC sources as they are. Mips of at most one tile form the tail, a plain image with mips. Writes are copied in submissions the host does not wait for, ordered before work submitted after them. Reference: J. M. P. van Waveren, "Software Virtual Textures", id Software, 2012.

More... #include <ernie/util/texture_bake.h> Public Functions Type Name std::uint64_t Encoded () const Texels of every mip encoded, and in all. const TextureData & Layout () const The stored texture's layout, its texels in the file only. RasterBake (const RasterBake &) = delete bool Step (std::uint64_t texels, bool wait=false) Encodes and writes what the reading thread has ready, about texels texels of it (a band's rows of blocks at least); with wait , waiting for it to be read. std::uint64_t Total () const RasterBake & operator= (const RasterBake &) = delete ~RasterBake () Stops the bake; an unfinished one removes its file. Detailed Description A thread of the bake's own reads the raster a part ( RasterSource::Parts ) and a band of 1024 rows at a time, as RGBA8, and makes the band's mips while they split into whole blocks at its edges, each the 2 x 2 average of the last (in linear light for sRGB colour), exactly the whole image's mips there. The smaller mips come from the bands' last ones joined. Step , on the caller's thread, encodes what is ready (on the GPU with the options' encoder) and writes it in place in the file. At most some 256 MB of band mips wait to be encoded. Samples are 8- or 16-bit (the high byte kept); one channel is grey, two grey and alpha, three RGB. References: * R. none for the camera's own exposure. virtual void SetViewportExposure (double stops) Stops on the viewport's photographic outputs ( Record ) on top of its camera's exposure, as a viewer's compensation asks; the viewport's frames meter their luminance too. virtual RenderStats Stats () const = 0 RenderProductSetOutputs Step (const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > products={}, const Path & settings={}, double deltaTime=0.0) StepAsync(...).Fetch() . virtual StepOperation StepAsync (const Scene & scene, std::span< const Path > products={}, const Path & settings={}, double deltaTime=0.0) = 0 Renders products of scene (see ResolveRenderProducts ) and returns at once: wait for or poll the operation, then fetch the outputs and map their render vars. virtual std::vector< TimelinePoint > SubmitWaits () const = 0 Semaphore waits the submission of commands from Record needs, for CUDA copies into the delegate's buffers that may still be running; empty without CUDA inputs. virtual void Sync (const Scene & scene) = 0 Uploads what changed in scene since the last call, or everything when scene is not the scene of the last call. double Time () const The sensor clock, seconds: where the last frame ended. virtual void Update (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings, VkExtent2D extent) = 0 Syncs, then prepares to draw the scene as the RenderSettings prim settings describes into an image of extent , for Record . virtual std::vector< std::string > ViewVars () const The render vars Record can draw of the frame the last Update prepared: Info() .viewVars and what that frame adds, such as the AOVs its sensor filters write ("aov:<name>"). virtual TextureWait WaitForTextures (const Scene & scene, double timeoutSeconds) Waits up to timeoutSeconds (infinity for no limit) for the textures scene 's materials read to load (they load in the background, ernie:textureLoading ), so that a program can render only once none is missing. RenderDelegate & operator= (const RenderDelegate &) = delete virtual ~RenderDelegate () = default Protected Functions Type Name FrameId NextFrame (const Scene & scene, const Path & settings, const Path & product) The frame of the next image of product (the settings' path for the interactive view): the ernie:frame of the resolved RenderSettings prim settings when authored, else how many images of the product this delegate rendered before; and the product's stream, StreamOf its path. RenderDelegate () = default TimeWindow TakeTimeWindow () Detailed Description The scene is the single source of truth. A delegate pulls its changes on Sync (each delegate keeps its own ChangeCursor ) and uploads only what changed, so there is no separate render index. Every backend reads the scene with the same resolution rules ( resolve.h ) and writes the same render vars through the camera's sensor filters ( sensor_filters.h ). There are two ways to render: * headless and in simulation: StepAsync (or Step and Render ) renders the UsdRender products of a scene and returns their render vars; * interactively: Update then Record into the application's own command buffer each frame, submitted after SubmitWaits . Rendering is deterministic: an image's noise and samples derive from the camera's ernie:sensor:seed , its render product's path and its frame number ( NextFrame ), so the same scene renders the same images on any machine and whatever else renders alongside. docs.text: The scene is the single source of truth. A delegate pulls its changes on Sync (each delegate keeps its own ChangeCursor ) and uploads only what changed, so there is no separate render index. Every backend reads the scene with the same resolution rules ( resolve.h ) and writes the same render vars through the camera's sensor filters ( sensor_filters.h ). There are two ways to render: * headless and in simulation: StepAsync (or Step and Render ) renders the UsdRender products of a scene and returns their render vars; * interactively: Update then Record into the application's own command buffer each frame, submitted after SubmitWaits . Rendering is deterministic: an image's noise and samples derive from the camera's ernie:sensor:seed , its render product's path and its frame number ( NextFrame ), so the same scene renders the same images on any machine and whatever else renders alongside.

Detailed Description Small values ( Value : scalars, vectors, matrices, tokens, relationships) are set one at a time; bulk data ( Tensor : heights, points, instance transforms) is written as tensors, either to one prim or as rows of one tensor spread over many prims without copying. On a prim of a registered type ( prim_type.h ), setting and writing check the attribute against its declaration ( Validate ): a misspelt name or a value of the wrong type throws, while custom attributes in namespaces of their own are free. Every edit advances Version() and stamps the prim's dirty bit for that attribute ( DirtyOf ); transform and visibility edits stamp the prim's descendants too. Each consumer keeps a ChangeCursor and calls Changes to get every prim changed since its last call, so several consumers can follow one scene independently. Changes costs O(prims). Defining a prim defines its missing ancestors as typeless prims, as UsdStage::DefinePrim does. The root / always exists, untyped. docs.text: Small values ( Value : scalars, vectors, matrices, tokens, relationships) are set one at a time; bulk data ( Tensor : heights, points, instance transforms) is written as tensors, either to one prim or as rows of one tensor spread over many prims without copying. On a prim of a registered type ( prim_type.h ), setting and writing check the attribute against its declaration ( Validate ): a misspelt name or a value of the wrong type throws, while custom attributes in namespaces of their own are free. Every edit advances Version() and stamps the prim's dirty bit for that attribute ( DirtyOf ); transform and visibility edits stamp the prim's descendants too. Each consumer keeps a ChangeCursor and calls Changes to get every prim changed since its last call, so several consumers can follow one scene independently. Changes costs O(prims). Defining a prim defines its missing ancestors as typeless prims, as UsdStage::DefinePrim does. The root / always exists, untyped. References: * Pixar, "UsdStage", https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_stage.html * Pixar, "HdChangeTracker" (dirty bits), https://openusd.org/release/api/class_hd_change_tracker.html

More... #include <ernie/scene/camera.h> Public Attributes Type Name int adcBits = 12 double blackLevelDn = 0.0 std::vector< SensorChannel > channels double darkCurrentElectrons = 0.1 Per second. double dsnuElectrons = /* multi line expression */ Standard deviation of the per-pixel offset. double electronsPerDnAtIso100 = /* multi line expression */ 0 means full well over the ADC range. double fullWellElectrons = 20000.0 bool noise = true double prnu = /* multi line expression */ Standard deviation of the relative gain. double readNoiseElectrons = 3.0 Standard deviation. std::uint32_t seed = 0 Public Functions Type Name double ElectronsPerDn (double iso) const Electrons per digital number at iso . Public Static Functions Type Name SensorModel Mono () One panchromatic channel with a front-illuminated silicon response, like the monochrome pushbroom cameras of lunar orbiters. SensorModel Rgb () Bayer-like red, green and blue channels behind an infrared cut filter. Detailed Description Electrons accumulate as photons times quantum efficiency, plus dark current; the readout adds photon shot noise (Poisson), read noise (Gaussian), and per-pixel fixed patterns PRNU (relative gain) and DSNU (offset); electrons clip at the full well, and the ADC converts them to digital numbers with the ISO-dependent gain, adds the black level and clips to its bit depth. The presets are generic curve shapes, not any particular sensor: replace the channels with measured curves for a specific camera. Reference: EMVA Standard 1288, "Standard for Characterization of Image Sensors and Cameras", release 4.0, 2021 (the linear camera model). Tiles have the format's standard block shape (64 KiB each: 128 x 128 texels of 32-bit texels, 256 x 256 of BC7). Mips smaller than a tile share the mip tail, bound at creation and written with WriteTail . Binding waits for the bind alone; texels are copied in submissions the host does not wait for, ordered before work submitted after them. docs.text: Shaders keep their samples to bound tiles by sampling no finer than the finest mip resident there ( VirtualTexture 's min-LOD map). Tiles have the format's standard block shape (64 KiB each: 128 x 128 texels of 32-bit texels, 256 x 256 of BC7). Mips smaller than a tile share the mip tail, bound at creation and written with WriteTail . Binding waits for the bind alone; texels are copied in submissions the host does not wait for, ordered before work submitted after them. Releasing unbinds at once: callers keep work in flight off the tiles they release ( VirtualTexture lets a frame pass first). Requires VulkanContext::SupportsSparseResidency . Reference: Khronos, "Sparse Resources", Vulkan specification, chapter 33. https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/sparsemem.html

Protected Functions inherited from ernie::SchemaView See ernie::SchemaView Type Name Scene & Edit () const The scene to edit. bool Has (std::string_view name) const SchemaView (const Scene & scene, Path path, const PrimTypeDef & type) SchemaView ( Scene & scene, Path path, const PrimTypeDef & type) Detailed Description They are attributes of the scene's root prim / , which stays untyped: the root's schema is this one, so Scene::Set checks them, edits are tracked and undone as any other, and scene files keep them under "/". The view is not a prim type ( PrimTypes ): no prim is defined as one. Fallbacks are what Ernie draws with: z up and metres, which USD's own fallbacks (y up, centimetres) are not, so a scene from USD states its units. Ernie records other units for interchange without converting them yet. The time code is the animation's clock, which an application sets as ovstage's apply_usd_time does ( SetTime , in seconds); a render delegate's sensor clock ( RenderDelegate::Time ), which its steps advance, is apart from it, so animation can hold or loop while sensors run on. References: * Pixar, "UsdStage" (stage metadata), https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_stage.html * Pixar, "Encoding Stage UpAxis" and "Encoding Stage Linear Units", https://openusd.org/release/api/group___usd_geom_up_axis__group.html * NVIDIA, ovstage ovstage_population_apply_usd_time . docs.text: They are attributes of the scene's root prim / , which stays untyped: the root's schema is this one, so Scene::Set checks them, edits are tracked and undone as any other, and scene files keep them under "/". The view is not a prim type ( PrimTypes ): no prim is defined as one. Fallbacks are what Ernie draws with: z up and metres, which USD's own fallbacks (y up, centimetres) are not, so a scene from USD states its units. Ernie records other units for interchange without converting them yet. The time code is the animation's clock, which an application sets as ovstage's apply_usd_time does ( SetTime , in seconds); a render delegate's sensor clock ( RenderDelegate::Time ), which its steps advance, is apart from it, so animation can hold or loop while sensors run on. References: * Pixar, "UsdStage" (stage metadata), https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_stage.html * Pixar, "Encoding Stage UpAxis" and "Encoding Stage Linear Units", https://openusd.org/release/api/group___usd_geom_up_axis__group.html * NVIDIA, ovstage ovstage_population_apply_usd_time . docs.text: Struct ernie::TemperatureModel ClassList > ernie > TemperatureModel A surface's temperature computed as it renders, written in Slang: what a thermal camera sees of a body whose temperatures follow its lighting, with no solver running beside the renderer (PANGU's approach). More... #include <ernie/scene/temperature_model.h> Public Attributes Type Name std::function< std::vector< float >()> defaultData = {} The data of materials that give none, made when one first needs it (the built-in diurnal 's lunar table); none without. std::string description std::string id The ernie:thermal:model naming it. std::string name std::vector< TemperatureModelParam > params std::vector< std::string > references std::string slang Its module's source. std::string typeName The Slang struct implementing it. Public Functions Type Name std::vector< float > Defaults () const Default value of every parameter, in order. Detailed Description A material names one in ernie:thermal:model ; its pixels take the model's temperature in place of the material's own, though a mesh's solver temperatures, a prim's and a temperature texture still win. slang is a Slang module that may import temperature_model; ( TemperatureModelSlang ) and defines a struct named typeName implementing ITemperatureModel , whose gives the temperature at a pixel from input : its point and outward surface normal (world, relative to the frame's origin); every distant light linked to it ( lightCount of them, at most kTemperatureLights , none singled out): its direction, its irradiance over all wavelengths facing it (W/m^2) and how much of it reaches the point past shadows; the sunlight on the surface from them all (W/m^2, shadowed); the pixel's solar absorptivity (the material's, scaled as its albedo textures scale its reflectance) and the material's thermal emissivity; its own temperature (0 for none); the frame's time (s); the world +z axis of a prim bound to the material (0 for none); and the pixel's thermal inertia (its thermal inertia texture's, else the material's; 0 for none). Parameter i is p.get(i) , the material's ernie:thermal:model:data p.data(i) ( p.dataCount() of them). docs.text: Requires Vulkan 1.3 with dynamic rendering, synchronization2, demote to helper invocation, timeline semaphores and shader draw parameters, plus push descriptors. Ray queries are enabled when the device supports them. Vulkan is loaded at run time through volk: the system loader on Linux and Windows, MoltenVK on macOS (with the portability extensions it needs). Several contexts may exist at once, on the same or different devices: core functions go through the loader's dispatch, and extension functions come from the context that enabled them (e.g. PushDescriptorSet ), never from volk's globals.

fields, such as a prim type's "Light" or "Shape" attributes. struct SequenceOptions A sequence to record ( Viewer::RecordSequence ). struct Theme Colours (sRGB-encoded with alpha, as written to the screen) and metrics of the viewer's UI: a classic scientific desktop look, as Qt's and GTK's of the 2000s that tools such as PANGU wear (colours read from PANGU v7's renderer GUI): light grey-green windows (#D4D7D0), white sunken fields and raised buttons with one-pixel edges, square corners, black text, a navy accent and pale-blue selection. class Timeline The animation's clock, as Omniverse Kit's timeline: plays the scene's time code ( Stage::GetTimeCode ) over the stage's range, from its start time code to its end, in real time or a frame at a time, looping or stopping at the end. class Viewer An interactive window onto an Ernie Scene : a docked viewport rendering the scene with a RenderDelegate (the rasterizer), plus Stage , Property, Render Settings, Sensor, Stats and Log panels. class ViewerLogs What the viewer's logging calls collect ( Viewer::LogScalar , LogArray , LogImage ), after Newton's viewers' log_scalar , log_array and log_image : scalar signals and arrays drawn in the Plots panel, and images each in a panel of its own, as textures the GPU samples where they were written. struct ViewerOptions Options for opening a Viewer . struct ViewportDisplay _What the viewport draws over the scene, as Kit's viewport "show by type" menu (the eye) and heads-up display settings choose._ class WidgetPanel A panel of simple widgets described by data rather than ImGui calls, so code without ImGui bindings (Python) can build one.

WidgetPanel & Widgets () The demo's controls in the Demos panel's Options section, as widgets (sliders, checkboxes, combos) rather than ImGui calls, as Python demos add theirs ( widgets ). Demo & operator= (const Demo &) = delete virtual ~Demo () Detailed Description Ernie's own demos derive from it, in C++ and in Python ( ernie.demo.Demo ), as may any application's. The scene is the viewer's, or one of the demo's own without a viewer. Give it a camera of its own, even for a demo meant for the viewer (which frames the scene with its own camera): without a viewer, and in tests ( RenderImage ), the scene renders through it. In the viewer a demo uses it as any application does ( Viewer::AddPanel , OnFrame , SetActiveCamera ...); when the Demos panel switches away, what it added is removed (in the demo's scope, Viewer::SetScope ) and the viewport's display settings are restored. docs.text: Ernie's own demos derive from it, in C++ and in Python ( ernie.demo.Demo ), as may any application's. The scene is the viewer's, or one of the demo's own without a viewer. Give it a camera of its own, even for a demo meant for the viewer (which frames the scene with its own camera): without a viewer, and in tests ( RenderImage ), the scene renders through it. In the viewer a demo uses it as any application does ( Viewer::AddPanel , OnFrame , SetActiveCamera ...); when the Demos panel switches away, what it added is removed (in the demo's scope, Viewer::SetScope ) and the viewport's display settings are restored. References: * Newton's examples ( newton.examples : Example , create_parser , init , run and the example browser), https://github.com/newton-physics/newton

docs.text: Class ernie::app::Timeline ClassList > ernie > app > Timeline The animation's clock, as Omniverse Kit's timeline: plays the scene's time code ( Stage::GetTimeCode ) over the stage's range, from its start time code to its end, in real time or a frame at a time, looping or stopping at the end. More... #include <ernie/app/timeline.h> Public Functions Type Name double Advance ( Scene & scene, double seconds) While playing, advances the time code by seconds of real time (a frame when playing every frame), from the range's start if it is outside it; past the end, loops or stops there. bool IsLooping () const Whether playing past the range's end starts over at its start; otherwise it stops at the end. bool IsPlaying () const void Pause () void Play () bool PlaysEveryFrame () const Whether playing advances a frame each step, whatever time the step took, so every frame is drawn once (capture, slow renders); otherwise playback keeps to real time. void Seek ( Scene & scene, double timeCode) Sets the time code to timeCode , playing or not. void SetLooping (bool looping) void SetPlayEveryFrame (bool everyFrame) void StepFrames ( Scene & scene, int frames) Pauses and moves frames frames on (back for negative ones), within the range. void Stop ( Scene & scene) Pauses, back at the range's start. Public Static Functions Type Name double FrameTimeCodes (const Scene & scene) Time codes in one frame: the stage's time codes per second over its frames per second. std::pair< double, double > Range (const Scene & scene) The range the timeline plays: the stage's start and end time codes, or, while the end is not past the start, 100 time codes from the start, as Kit's new stages hold. double TimeCode (const Scene & scene) The time code the scene's animation is at. Detailed Description It writes the time code into the scene's root, as an application sets it, outside the undo history; the renderer's sensor clock is apart from it. Time codes run at the stage's time codes per second; a frame is the stage's frames per second's share of a second of them. Reference: NVIDIA, Omniverse Kit omni.timeline (play, pause, stop, looping, play every frame). docs.text: Class ernie::app::Viewer ClassList > ernie > app > Viewer An interactive window onto an Ernie Scene : a docked viewport rendering the scene with a RenderDelegate (the rasterizer), plus Stage , Property, Render Settings, Sensor, Stats and Log panels. More... #include <ernie/app/viewer.h> Public Types Type Name enum Exposure How the viewport exposes its image: Auto keys the scene's metered average luminance to middle grey (adapting over a fraction of a second), Camera (the default) takes the camera's own exposure attributes as they are, and Default is automatic through the viewer's own camera and the camera's own through a scene camera. enum Gizmo What the transform gizmo on a single selected prim does: none, or translate, rotate or scale (the W, E and R keys), in world or local axes. Public Functions Type Name const Path & ActiveCamera () const The Camera prim the viewport looks through; PerspectiveCamera() until changed. std::uint64_t AddHudItem (std::string label, std::function< std::string( Viewer &)> value, bool shown=true) Adds a line to the viewport's heads-up display, "label: value" with the text value returns (asked a few times a second), such as a physics step's time; the eye menu's Heads Up Display submenu toggles it. void AddMenuItem (const std::string & menu, const std::string & label, std::function< void( Viewer &)> action) Adds label to the menu bar's menu (created if needed), running action when chosen. std::uint64_t AddOverlayClickHandler (std::function< void( Viewer &, const std::string &, std::uint32_t)> clicked) Calls clicked with the overlay's name and the item's id when a click in the viewport lands on a screen overlay item with an id ( OverlayStyle::id , such as a button's, Overlay::Button ), in place of picking the scene there. std::uint64_t AddOverlayPickHandler (std::function< void( Viewer &, const OverlayHit &)> picked) Calls picked when a click in the viewport lands on an overlay item in the world (a marker, a line, a batch's item; OverlayHit ), as the renderer picks it, in place of picking the scene there. Panel & AddPanel (std::unique_ptr< Panel > panel) Adds a dockable panel, shown under Window in the menu bar. T & AddPanel (Args &&... args) Constructs a T (a Panel subclass) from args and adds it; returns it. Panel & AddPanel (std::string title, Dock dock, std::function< void( Viewer &)> draw) Adds a panel titled title that calls draw to draw its contents with Dear ImGui; for panels that need no class of their own. std::uint64_t AddViewportMenuItem (std::string label, std::function< void( Viewer &)> action, std::function< bool(const Viewer &)> checked={}) Adds label to the viewport's settings menu (its leftmost pill), running action when chosen; with checked , the item shows a check mark while it returns true. std::uint64_t AddViewportToggle (std::string label, bool shown=true, std::string overlay={}, std::function< void( Viewer &, bool)> changed={}) Adds a toggle to the viewport's eye menu, after the built-in ones, for what an application draws over the scene, such as physics contacts or labels. WidgetPanel & AddWidgetPanel (std::string title, Dock dock=Dock::Right) Adds a WidgetPanel titled title , for widgets added without ImGui (Python's panels). bool AutoExposing () const Whether the viewport currently exposes automatically ( Exposure ). const BrdfRegistry & Brdfs () const The reflectance models of the current backend, for material editors. Path CameraFromView (const Path & path) Defines a Camera prim at path in the scene with the active camera's transform and lens, and returns it. std::vector< Path > Cameras () const The cameras the viewport can look through: the viewer's own, then the scene's Camera prims by path. void Capture (const std::filesystem::path & path, std::string var={}) Writes the next viewport frame to path as PNG, showing var (the shown var when empty) as the viewport draws it, and on screen for that frame. void CaptureWindow (const std::filesystem::path & path) Writes the whole window as last drawn, UI and all, to path as PNG: for screenshot tests of the interface. void ClearAttribute (const Path & path, std::string_view attribute) Clears attribute of the prim at path , back to its fallback, as an undoable GUI edit. void ClearLog () void ClearScene () Empties the stage for new content: removes every prim but the viewer's own and every overlay but the viewer's (named with a leading "__"), clears the selection and undo history, and forgets the settings, camera and lighting the application chose. bool ClockPaused () const Whether the sensor clock ( RenderDelegate::AdvanceTime ) stands still between frames; by default it runs with them, a frame's seconds a frame, so pulses and pattern sequences play out. void Close () Asks the window to close; Run returns and Step returns false after the current frame. VulkanContext & Context () const VulkanContext & Context () const Path Create (std::string_view type) Creates a prim of type , any of the Create menu's ( CreatableTypes ), with defaults that make it show ( AuthorDefaultPrim ): under the selected Xform or Scope if one is, else its type's usual parent, at the view's target and scale. RenderDelegate & Delegate () The current backend itself, for what the viewer does not wrap, such as CUDA bindings. void Delete (std::span< const Path > paths) Deletes the prims at paths and their descendants as one undo step and clears the selection; the viewer's own prims are left alone. std::vector< Path > Duplicate (std::span< const Path > paths) Copies the prims at paths with their descendants and attributes (sharing tensors) beside themselves, named <name>_01 , <name>_02 ... with the first free number, as one undo step (Ctrl+D); selects and returns the copies. bool EcoPaused () const Whether eco mode ( RenderSettings __ ernie:ecoMode:enabled , as Omniverse's) has paused the viewport's rendering, nothing it shows having changed for ernie:ecoMode:maxFramesWithoutChange frames; it keeps its last image until something does. void Edit (const Path & path, std::string_view attribute, Value value, bool open=false) Sets attribute of the prim at path as a GUI edit, through the viewer's undo history ( History ). void EditLocalTransform (const Path & path, const glm::dmat4 & local, bool open=false) Gives the prim at path the local transform local as a GUI edit, as Edit does, through its own transform ops where they can represent it ( LocalTransformEdits ). bool Encoding () const Whether a recorded sequence's video is still encoding. double ExposureCompensation () const Stops of exposure compensation on top of either mode, in the viewport only ( RenderDelegate::SetViewportExposure ): the camera's exposure and the products' outputs are untouched. Panel * FindPanel (std::string_view title) The panel titled title , built-in ("Stats") or added; null if there is none. void FocusPanel (std::string_view title) Shows the panel titled title and brings it to the front: where it shares a dock with other panels its tab becomes the selected one, and it takes keyboard focus. void Frame (std::span< const Path > paths={}) Frames paths (the whole scene when empty) with the active camera (the F key). CaptureOptions & GetCaptureOptions () Where screenshots and sequences go (the Capture panel). Exposure GetExposure () const FileDialog & GetFileDialog () The file dialog, open or not: for choosing through it from code, as tests do. Gizmo GetGizmo () const Lighting GetLighting () const std::optional< bool > GetMinimal () const Whether the viewport shades minimally ( ernie:minimal:mode , Kit's "RTX - Minimal"): true for the surfaces' diffuse colours, false for full shading, overriding the render settings in the viewport only; or none (the default) to follow them. Scene & GetScene () const Theme & GetTheme () const Timeline & GetTimeline () The animation's timeline (the Timeline panel, Space to play and pause), which each frame advances before the frame callbacks run ( FrameInfo::timeCode ). const Timeline & GetTimeline () const const ViewportDisplay & GetViewportDisplay () const What the viewport draws over the scene and its heads-up display lists. bool GetVsync () const Whether frames wait for the display's refresh ( ViewerOptions::vsync ); without it the viewer draws as fast as it renders, without tearing where the display allows. std::optional< Wireframe > GetWireframe () const How the viewport draws triangle edges: a mode overriding the render settings' own ( ernie:wireframe ) in the viewport only, or none (the default) to follow them. bool GizmoLocal () const EditHistory & History () The GUI edits, for undo and redo. bool HudItemShown (std::uint64_t id) const bool IsOpen () const Whether the window is open. void LoadLayout (const std::filesystem::path & path) void Log ( LogLevel level, std::string text) Adds a message to the viewer's log, shown in the Log panel; the viewer itself logs render errors as they start. void LogArray (std::string_view name, const Tensor & array, std::uintptr_t stream=1) Logs array , (n) or (rows, cols) numbers on the host or the GPU, as a heatmap in the Plots panel, replacing the last; a GPU array is downloaded after the work queued on compute stream stream . const std::deque< LogEntry > & LogEntries () const void LogImage (std::string_view name, const Tensor & image, std::uintptr_t stream=1) Logs image in a panel of its own titled name , replacing the last: (rows, cols), (rows, cols, channels) or a batch (views, rows, cols, channels), with 1, 3 or 4 channels, uint8 (0 to 255, shown as they are, so sRGB) or float32 (0 to 1). void LogScalar (std::string_view name, double value, bool clear=false, int smoothing=1) Logging, after Newton's viewers' log_scalar , log_array and log_image : values a simulation or sensor produces, shown live as they change. std::vector< double > LoggedScalars (std::string_view name) const The samples of scalar signal name so far, oldest first; empty if none. void LookAt (const glm::dvec3 & eye, const glm::dvec3 & target) Puts the active camera at eye looking at target (z up), which it then orbits and zooms towards: a view from a chosen distance, where Frame fits the whole prim. Tensor MapImage (std::string_view name, std::vector< std::int64_t > shape, DType type, std::uintptr_t stream=1) The texture of the image panel name itself, as a tensor of shape and type (as LogImage takes them, without 3 channels) on the viewer's GPU, its rows the texture's pitch apart: write it on compute stream stream and UnmapImage , and the panel shows it with no copy at all. std::optional< double > MeteredEv () const The EV100 of the scene's average luminance as last metered (EV = log2(L x 100 / 12.5)), if the backend meters. bool MinimalShown () const Whether the viewport shades minimally now, by GetMinimal or else the render settings. std::uint64_t NewScope () Registration scopes, for applications that host others' code, as the demo runner hosts demos: what is added (callbacks, panels, menu items, viewport toggles, heads-up display and viewport menu items) belongs to the scope current when it is added, and RemoveScope removes all of it at once. std::uint64_t OnFrame (std::function< void( Viewer &, const FrameInfo &)> callback) Adds a callback run at the start of every frame, before the UI and the render, so its edits show in that frame. std::uint64_t OnPostRender (std::function< void( Viewer &, const FrameInfo &)> callback) Adds a callback run after the frame is submitted and presented; the GPU may still be rendering it. std::uint64_t OnPreRender (std::function< void( Viewer &, const FrameInfo &)> callback) Adds a callback run after the UI and just before the scene is synced and rendered: the scene then holds this frame's GUI edits, and the callback's own edits show in this frame. std::uint64_t OnSelection (std::function< void( Viewer &, std::span< const Path >)> callback) Adds a callback run when the selection changes, by click or by SetSelection . std::uint64_t OnUi (std::function< void( Viewer &, const FrameInfo &)> callback) Adds a callback run during the UI, after the panels, inside the Dear ImGui frame: for keyboard shortcuts ( ImGui::IsKeyPressed ) and overlays. void OpenFileDialog ( FileDialogOptions options, std::function< void( Viewer &, const std::filesystem::path &)> done) Opens the viewer's file dialog ( FileDialog ), modal over the window, to choose a file to open or to save as options says. void OpenScene (const std::filesystem::path & path) Replaces the stage with the scene the JSON file at path describes ( LoadSceneFile , ernie/scene/scene_json.h ), as File > Open > Scene > does: empties the stage ( > ClearScene > ), loads the file and starts the session over ( ResetSession ). Detailed Description The viewer keeps no scene state of its own: panels read the scene each frame and write edits back through Scene::Set , so edits from code and from the GUI are one history, seen by both. What only the GUI needs (its cameras, the viewport's render product, lighting presets) is defined under SessionRoot() , which panels hide unless asked to show it. The viewer defines its own perspective camera on opening, framing the scene ( PerspectiveCamera() , the default view). The viewport looks through it or any Camera prim of the scene; navigating moves whichever camera it looks through. Drive it in one of two ways, both on the thread that created it (GLFW needs the main thread on macOS): * Run() loops until the window closes; * Step() draws one frame and returns, for callers that own the loop, such as a simulation. Each frame runs, in order: OnFrame callbacks; the UI, whose panels may edit the scene, then OnUi callbacks; OnPreRender callbacks; the scene's sync and render, and presentation; OnPostRender callbacks. Callbacks run on the viewer's thread; an exception from one ends that frame and propagates out of Step or Run , and the viewer can step again afterwards. Applications extend it with panels ( AddPanel ), menu items ( AddMenuItem ) and callbacks; TerrainGen's viewer is one such application, adding its terrain configuration panels. docs.text: The viewer keeps no scene state of its own: panels read the scene each frame and write edits back through Scene::Set , so edits from code and from the GUI are one history, seen by both. What only the GUI needs (its cameras, the viewport's render product, lighting presets) is defined under SessionRoot() , which panels hide unless asked to show it. The viewer defines its own perspective camera on opening, framing the scene ( PerspectiveCamera() , the default view). The viewport looks through it or any Camera prim of the scene; navigating moves whichever camera it looks through. Drive it in one of two ways, both on the thread that created it (GLFW needs the main thread on macOS): * Run() loops until the window closes; * Step() draws one frame and returns, for callers that own the loop, such as a simulation. Each frame runs, in order: OnFrame callbacks; the UI, whose panels may edit the scene, then OnUi callbacks; OnPreRender callbacks; the scene's sync and render, and presentation; OnPostRender callbacks. Callbacks run on the viewer's thread; an exception from one ends that frame and propagates out of Step or Run , and the viewer can step again afterwards. Applications extend it with panels ( AddPanel ), menu items ( AddMenuItem ) and callbacks; TerrainGen's viewer is one such application, adding its terrain configuration panels.

docs.text: Namespace ernie::profiler Namespace List > ernie > profiler Summaries of the profiler's frames ( ernie/util/profiler.h ) as Omniverse Kit's profiler window shows them: each zone nested in the zone that encloses it, with its time averaged over the frames, its share of the frame, and exports as text, JSON and a Chrome trace. More... Classes Type Name struct Frame One frame's zones. struct Report The GPU's zones and the CPU's, the latter under a node per thread. struct ReportFilter What to list of a report: zones nested at most depth deep (0: the outermost alone) and taking at least minMs , in a tree whose siblings come in the order they ran or, byTime , longest first. struct ReportNode A zone's averages over the frames summarized: zones of the same name under the same parent merge. struct ReportRow A listed zone and how deep it is shown. class ScopedZone Times the rest of the enclosing scope as a CPU zone named name while recording. struct Zone A timed span: a CPU zone of thread thread , or a GPU zone ( thread unused) on the device's own clock. Public Attributes Type Name constexpr std::size_t kFramesInFlight = 2 The newest frames whose GPU zones may have arrived in part: the device still runs their commands, and a zone arrives once its own commands have run, before the zones around it end. Public Functions Type Name void AddGpuZone (std::uint64_t frame, const Zone & zone) Adds a GPU zone recorded during frame frame ; dropped if that frame is no longer kept. void BeginFrame () Ends the current frame and starts the next; the ended frame joins Frames (whether recording or not, so frame times show even before any zones). void Clear () bool CpuEnabled () std::uint64_t CurrentFrame () The index of the frame being recorded. bool Enabled () std::vector< Frame > Frames () The finished frames kept, oldest first, at most History of them. bool GpuEnabled () std::size_t History () const char * Intern (std::string_view name) A copy of name that lives as long as the process, for zones named at run time (zones keep their name's pointer); the same pointer for the same name. std::uint64_t Now () Nanoseconds on the steady clock. std::string ReportJson (const Report & report) The report as JSON: {"gpu": {"ms", "zones": [...]}, "cpu": ...}, each zone {"name", "ms", "calls", "percent", "children"}. std::string ReportText (const Report & report, const ReportFilter & filter) The report as lines of indented names, times and shares. std::vector< ReportRow > Rows (const std::vector< ReportNode > & nodes, const ReportFilter & filter) The rows of nodes that filter lists, parents before their children. void SetCpuEnabled (bool enabled) Starts or stops recording CPU zones ( ERNIE_ZONE ) alone, or GPU zones ( ERNIE_GPU_ZONE ) alone. void SetEnabled (bool enabled) Starts or stops recording CPU and GPU zones both; stopping keeps the frames recorded so far. void SetGpuEnabled (bool enabled) void SetHistory (std::size_t frames) void SetThreadName (std::string name) Report Summarize (std::span< const Frame > frames, const std::vector< std::string > & threadNames) Averages frames ' zones; threadNames names the CPU's threads by index ( ThreadNames ). std::uint32_t ThreadIndex () The calling thread's index in Zone::thread , and the names threads gave themselves ( SetThreadName , else "Thread <index>"), by index. std::vector< std::string > ThreadNames () std::string TraceJson (std::span< const Frame > frames, const std::vector< std::string > & threadNames) frames in the Trace Event Format: a complete event per zone, the CPU's threads as threads of process 1 and the GPU's zones as process 2, times in microseconds from the first frame. Detailed Description Ernie's in-process profiler: the zones of ERNIE_ZONE and ERNIE_GPU_ZONE ( ernie/util/profile.h , ernie/device/gpu_profile.h ) recorded frame by frame for a profiler panel, alongside Tracy's (which streams them to its own viewer in a profiling build). References: * NVIDIA, "Profiling", Omniverse Kit SDK manual (the Profiler window: GPU and CPU zone trees, depths, averaging, exports). https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/kit-manual/latest/guide/profiling.html * Google, "Trace Event Format" (complete events, "ph": "X", and thread-name metadata), read by Perfetto and chrome://tracing. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CvAClvFfyA5R-PhYUmn5OOQtYMH4h6I0nSsKchNAySU Recording is off until SetEnabled ; while off a zone costs one atomic load. A frame runs from one BeginFrame to the next: CPU zones belong to the frame in which they end, GPU zones to the frame in which their commands were recorded (they arrive later, once the device has run them). The latest frames are kept, oldest first ( Frames ). docs.text: Ernie's in-process profiler: the zones of ERNIE_ZONE and ERNIE_GPU_ZONE ( ernie/util/profile.h , ernie/device/gpu_profile.h ) recorded frame by frame for a profiler panel, alongside Tracy's (which streams them to its own viewer in a profiling build). References: * NVIDIA, "Profiling", Omniverse Kit SDK manual (the Profiler window: GPU and CPU zone trees, depths, averaging, exports). https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/kit-manual/latest/guide/profiling.html * Google, "Trace Event Format" (complete events, "ph": "X", and thread-name metadata), read by Perfetto and chrome://tracing. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CvAClvFfyA5R-PhYUmn5OOQtYMH4h6I0nSsKchNAySU Recording is off until SetEnabled ; while off a zone costs one atomic load. A frame runs from one BeginFrame to the next: CPU zones belong to the frame in which they end, GPU zones to the frame in which their commands were recorded (they arrive later, once the device has run them). The latest frames are kept, oldest first ( Frames ).

docs.text: File gpu_profile.h File List > device > gpu_profile.h Go to the documentation of this file // SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause #pragma once // GPU zones: the time a command buffer spends between a zone's start // and end on the device, recorded by Ernie's own profiler // (ernie/util/profiler.h, through the context's `GpuTimer`) for the // viewer's Profiler panel while it records, and in a profiling build // (ERNIE_TRACY) also sent to Tracy on the same timeline as the CPU // zones of ernie/util/profile.h. // // // Until the end of the scope. // ERNIE_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, "Shadow passes"); // // A name chosen at run time, which must outlive the profile // // (a string literal, such as a drawable's `ProfileName`). // ERNIE_GPU_ZONE_NAMED(context, commands, // drawable.ProfileName()); // // Finished zones reach the profilers when later command buffers // collect them (`VulkanContext::CollectGpuProfile`, which `Submit` // and `SubmitAsync` do). // // References: // - B. Taudul, "Tracy Profiler", the Vulkan GPU zones // (TracyVulkan.hpp). https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy #include "ernie/device/vulkan_context.h" #include "ernie/util/profile.h" namespace ernie { class ScopedGpuZone { public: ScopedGpuZone(const VulkanContext& context, VkCommandBuffer commands, const char* name) : timer_(context.Timer()), commands_(commands), zone_(timer_.Begin(commands, name)) {} ~ScopedGpuZone() { timer_.End(commands_, zone_); } ScopedGpuZone(const ScopedGpuZone&) = delete; ScopedGpuZone& operator=(const ScopedGpuZone&) = delete; private: GpuTimer& timer_; VkCommandBuffer commands_; std::int64_t zone_; }; } // namespace ernie #define ERNIE_OWN_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) \ const ::ernie::ScopedGpuZone ERNIE_PROFILE_CONCAT( \ ernieOwnGpuZone, __LINE__)((context), (commands), name) #if ERNIE_TRACY // volk first: TracyVulkan.hpp calls Vulkan through volk's function // pointers. #include <volk.h> #include <tracy/TracyVulkan.hpp> #define ERNIE_GPU_PROFILER(context) \ static_cast<tracy::VkCtx*>((context).GpuProfiler()) #define ERNIE_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) \ TracyVkNamedZone(ERNIE_GPU_PROFILER(context), \ TracyConcat(ernieGpuZone, TracyLine), commands, \ name, ERNIE_GPU_PROFILER(context) != nullptr); \ ERNIE_OWN_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) #define ERNIE_GPU_ZONE_NAMED(context, commands, name) \ TracyVkZoneTransient(ERNIE_GPU_PROFILER(context), \ TracyConcat(ernieGpuZone, TracyLine), \ commands, name, \ ERNIE_GPU_PROFILER(context) != nullptr); \ ERNIE_OWN_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) #else #define ERNIE_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) \ ERNIE_OWN_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) #define ERNIE_GPU_ZONE_NAMED(context, commands, name) \ ERNIE_OWN_GPU_ZONE(context, commands, name) #endif

Classes Type Name struct CameraParams A camera's parameters resolved from its Camera prim ( CameraParamsOf ): a physically based pinhole camera for one image, with UsdGeomCamera's pose, projection and exposure attributes, a spectral range, a lens and a sensor. struct CameraView The raster view of a camera for one frame, derived from a CameraParams by CameraParams::RasterView : what the rasterizer's passes need. struct LensModel A lens: its projection, natural vignetting and transmission. struct LensRayTable A lens given as its rays: unit directions in the camera's frame at every step th sensor pixel corner, ( width / step + 1) by ( height / step + 1) of them row by row from the top left, interpolated between. struct Polarizer A camera's linear polarizer ( tokens::kPolarizerType ): none, one in front of the lens at angle (radians from the image's +x towards +y), or a polarization sensor's mosaic of 2 x 2 pixels at 90, 45 / 135, 0 degrees (Sony's IMX250MZR). struct SensorChannel One channel of a sensor: its quantum efficiency (electrons per photon) over wavelength. struct SensorModel An image sensor: channels with quantum efficiency curves, full well, noise, gain and ADC. docs.text: Type Name struct CameraParams A camera's parameters resolved from its Camera prim ( CameraParamsOf ): a physically based pinhole camera for one image, with UsdGeomCamera's pose, projection and exposure attributes, a spectral range, a lens and a sensor. struct CameraView The raster view of a camera for one frame, derived from a CameraParams by CameraParams::RasterView : what the rasterizer's passes need. struct LensModel A lens: its projection, natural vignetting and transmission. struct LensRayTable A lens given as its rays: unit directions in the camera's frame at every step th sensor pixel corner, ( width / step + 1) by ( height / step + 1) of them row by row from the top left, interpolated between. struct Polarizer A camera's linear polarizer ( tokens::kPolarizerType ): none, one in front of the lens at angle (radians from the image's +x towards +y), or a polarization sensor's mosaic of 2 x 2 pixels at 90, 45 / 135, 0 degrees (Sony's IMX250MZR). struct SensorChannel One channel of a sensor: its quantum efficiency (electrons per photon) over wavelength. struct SensorModel An image sensor: channels with quantum efficiency curves, full well, noise, gain and ADC. Classes Type Name class IsdCameraModel What usgscsm's camera models of image support data share, in the body-fixed frame in metres: struct FrameView A frame of the detector as Ernie renders it: a frame camera of the image's samples by its rows, posed ( camera.transform , camera to body-fixed world) when the frame is exposed, the lens's distortion fitted as Brown-Conrady terms (and scale). class IsdFrame A frame camera from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's frame model ( UsgsAstroFrameSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): the whole image is exposed at once, at the ISD's centre time, from one position and orientation. class IsdLineScanner A line scanner (pushbroom camera) from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's line scanner model ( UsgsAstroLsSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): line l is exposed around its time ImageTime(l) , a rate's start time plus its seconds per line times (l - its start line + 0.5), through detector line 0. struct Strip A strip of lines image lines from firstLine as Ernie renders it: a pushbroom camera ( CameraParams::pushbroom ) whose rows are those lines, posed from at the strip's first line's start and to at its end (camera to body-fixed world). class IsdPushFrame A push-frame camera (LROC's WAC, MRO's MARCI) from its image support data, its geometry as usgscsm's push-frame model ( UsgsAstroPushFrameSensorModel ) computes it ( IsdCameraModel ): the image is a stack of framelets, each a frame of FrameletLines lines exposed at once. struct Framelet Framelet __ framelet (in image order, from the top) as Ernie renders it: a frame camera of the image's samples by FrameletLines lines, posed when it is exposed (camera to body-fixed world), its exposure the ISD's, the lens's distortion fitted as Brown-Conrady terms (and scale). struct IsdRotation A rotation sampled over time between two NAIF frames, as ALE reads it ( ale::Orientations ): quaternions (w, x, y, z, scalar first) of the time-dependent rotation of vectors from the reference frame into the first of timeDependentFrames , and a constant rotation (row-major, applied to vectors after it) on into the first of constantFrames . struct IsdSamples <typename T> States sampled over time: ephemeris times (seconds past J2000, TDB) and a value at each. struct IsdSensor A camera's image support data (ISD) in the Community Sensor Model's JSON form, as ALE (the USGS Abstraction Layer for Ephemerides) writes it from SPICE kernels for planetary cameras such as LRO's NAC and WAC, MRO's CTX and HiRISE: the image's size and timing, the focal plane's map to detector pixels, the optics, and the spacecraft's and the body's states over the image. Classes Type Name class Overlay A named layer of debug drawing: lines, shapes, markers and labels in world coordinates or posed under prims ( OverlayStyle::anchor ), and text and panels on the image itself ( Text , Rect ), drawn over the images of render products that ask for it ( tokens::kOverlays ), after the sensor filters, so they never reach observations that do not. struct OverlayBatch Many overlay items of one kind from arrays on the host or a GPU ( Overlay::Batch ), such as one per world of a batched simulation, or a physics engine's bodies, contacts and particles: the renderer reads the arrays as they are, without copies to the host, and draws each item from them on the GPU. struct OverlayFont struct OverlayGlyph One character of the font ( OverlayTextFont ). struct OverlayHit What a pick of a rendered image found at a pixel ( RenderDelegate::PickOverlay ): the overlay drawing it, and in it a batch's item ( batch the batch, item its index) or a host item ( batch -1, item its OverlayStyle::id ). struct OverlayItem What every overlay item carries besides its geometry. struct OverlayNumberFormat How a Numbers batch prints each of its values: prefix , the value with decimals digits after the point, then suffix , in the style's colour and size , over its background . struct OverlaySegment A line segment of width pixels, dashed every dash pixels ( OverlayStyle::dash ) unless 0. struct OverlaySprite A rectangle facing the image at a fixed size in pixels, placed by a world point: rect spans (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) pixels from where anchor projects, y down. struct OverlayStyle How overlay items look. struct OverlayTriangle A filled triangle. struct ScreenPlacement Where a screen item ( Overlay::Text , Overlay::Rect ) sits on the image, whatever its size: the point at (fractions of the image's width and height from its top left corner) moved offset pixels (y down), with the item's own point align (fractions of its width and height from its top left) there. prims as rows of one array, as a simulation keeps its bodies' poses: written whole from any array (CPU or CUDA, DLPack, no copy), or mapped and written in place on the device asked for, each write one change ( ColumnChange ) whatever the number of prims. struct ColumnChange One attribute of many prims written whole as rows of one tensor ( Scene::Write of a PrimSet again, or Scene::Unmap of it) renderer's interop buffers: a column mapped there ( Column::Map ) is then written where the consumer reads it, copying nothing. struct Rows Rows a consumer offers, and whether they are storage it keeps (mapped again, the same rows) rather than a copy made there for now. class Prim Handle to a prim in a Scene : its path plus the scene, for chained edits. class PrimSet A fixed list of prims to write rows of one tensor to at once ( Scene::Write ), such as a simulation's bodies every step: the scene looks the prims up the first time and keeps them, looking them up again only after prims are removed or for another scene. class Scene A lightweight, USD-shaped scene for Ernie: a tree of typed prims named by Path , each holding attributes by USD name, plus change tracking for render delegates. struct Bound Attributes that are rows of a column ( columns_ ): which, its row, and the column's version its tensors last took ( Refresh ), so a column written whole costs its prims nothing until read. class Selection The prims of a type that hold some attributes ( Scene::Select ), as a Fabric query finds the buckets of a type and attributes: found again only once prims of the type come, go, or author or clear an attribute, and kept in one PrimSet meanwhile, so the columns of its attributes stay theirs from step to step. docs.text: Volumes as reflected schemas ( prim_type.h ), after UsdVol: a Volume names its fields with field:<name> relationships (an open namespace), and each field is a prim of its own, such as an OpenVDBAsset naming a grid of a NanoVDB file. #define ERNIE_FIELD_ASSET_ATTRIBUTES ( X ) `/* multi line expression */` How the fields shade is the Volume's bound Material's volume inputs ( material_schemas.h ). Reference: Pixar, UsdVol, https://openusd.org/release/api/usd_vol_page_front.html
